Abrego Garcia, 31, was arrested in Baltimore in March 2025 and deported to a Salvadoran prison notorious for abusive conditions and alleged use of torture.
The Trump administration, at the time, described Abrego Garcia’s deportation as an “administrative error”. However, the administration initially refused to seek his return, arguing that Abrego Garcia was a member of the MS-13 gang despite having no criminal record at the time of his removal.
In June 2025 , the Trump administration brought him back after facing public pressure and a court order, but only after securing an indictment charging him with human smuggling in Tennessee .
The Tennessee case was dismissed by a federal judge in May, though the government appealed it in August .
Abrego Garcia had said that if he must be deported, he would prefer to be sent to Costa Rica, but Todd Lyons, the former acting director of US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE), said that deporting him to Costa Rica would be “prejudicial to the United States” in a March 2026 memo.

Russia has kept the death toll of its soldiers in the Ukraine war a carefully guarded secret. Now documents leaked to the Guardian have revealed its true scale . The Guardian’s Russia affairs correspondent, Pjotr Sauer , tells Helen Pidd what reporters have discovered.
Two groups of hackers accessed Russia’s main statistics database last month and discovered a cache of 11m death certificates that revealed nearly 500,000 Russian losses in Ukraine since 2022. Among these were 1,000 – the equivalent of a whole regiment – who took their own lives.
The documents show how the majority of soldiers come from poorer areas and ethnic minorities, drawn in by high salaries. There are also recruits from abroad and even those lured to Russia by offers of jobs. But for how long can Vladimir Putin keep this shocking death toll from the Russian people?
texts.https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cmx2:
At least 490,334 Russian soldiers have died since the start of the war in Ukraine in 2022, according to Russian government statistics analysed by the BBC.
The leaked Rosstat data reveal how the full-scale invasion of Ukraine has fundamentally changed mortality patterns in Russia, and show the high cost paid in human life in a war that Vladimir Putin had assumed would last only days but is now almost five years old.
BBC Russian has had access to more than 11 million death records from 2021 to September 2026, after a hack by Belarusian group Cyber Partisans BY and Ukraine's Silent Crow.
Russia's statistics agency admitted to a cyber-attack, but denied any protected information had been leaked.
Together with independent Russian outlet Mediazona, BBC Russian has compared the Rosstat data with its own list of confirmed military deaths, pulled from open sources since the start of the invasion, and it has found matches for 90% of the records.
Military experts estimate that the BBC's list of 290,012 deaths, gleaned from official reports, social media, new memorials and graves, may account for 45-55% of the true death toll, which would range from 527,295 to 644,471.
The records show that 65% of 18 to 24 year-olds in Russia who lost their lives in 2025 died in the war. For those aged 25-34 the number was 59%. Only among 45 to 54 year-olds does cardiovascular disease claim more Russian lives than the conflict.
The data also reveal the extent of losses in specific areas of Ukraine. Some 20,000 Russian soldiers died fighting for control of 10 Ukrainian villages whose combined pre-war population was 12,000.
During the fight for one small village called Andriivka, south of the town of Bakhmut in Donetsk region, 1,122 Russians lost their lives. Before the war 74 people lived there.
Russia does not give public figures for losses sustained since the war began in February 2022. And two years ago Rosstat stopped publishing data of deaths from external causes, which was used to gauge the extent of military losses.
For example, only 70% of deaths we have established of soldiers from the occupied regions of Donetsk and Luhansk in eastern Ukraine who fought in the Russian army were accounted for in the Rosstat files.
Overall, the Rosstat dataset confirms the trends that we have observed with our own count.
Ukrainian losses were last put at about 50,000 by President Volodymyr Zelensky in July 2026, but another list based on open sources by the anonymous UA Losses website puts the figure at 115,952.
The Rosstat dataset contains no names but does include ages, places of residence, places of death and also circumstances of death.
We have filtered the records first by location, leaving only Ukraine as well as Russian border regions that saw incursions by the Ukrainian army.
Next, we identified 425,174 entries explicitly indicating a military-related cause of death, such as explosions or shrapnel during combat operations.
As this count could include civilians, we filtered out women as well as men outside the 18-65 age group. And if someone lived and died in the four Ukrainian regions occupied by Russia, we excluded them as a possible civilian – unless he had a record of military service attached to his entry.
Another 14,093 entries were identified by looking at employment, and 51,067 were recorded in the database as deceased on the basis of a court ruling. This often happens when a soldier goes missing in a combat zone for more than six months and their body has not been recovered.
Again, we filtered out civilians by only counting deaths in the war zones in Ukraine and Russia.
According to BBC Russian's analysis of the leaked files, in the first year of the war the average age of those killed was 34. By 2025, as prisoners and contract soldiers entered the ranks, it had risen to 40 (38 according to our own list).
Some of Russia's poorest regions in Eastern Siberia account for a disproportionately large share of the losses. Men from Tyva, Buryatia and Zabaykalsky Krai are 20-25 times more likely to die in the war than residents of the biggest cities of Moscow and St Petersburg.
In most regions, the distribution of deaths based on Rosstat data differs from that in the BBC's list by just a few tenths of a percentage point.
At least 5,017 foreigners are among those who died fighting for Russia, according to our analysis of the Rosstat files, including 1,031 Uzbeks and 720 Tajiks. We have left out Ukrainians from this count to avoid including civilians.
This is a conservative estimate as dual nationals are listed as Russians in the database, and there is no reference to North Koreans who died repelling the Ukrainian incursion into Russia in 2024.
The BBC identified 2,304 North Korean soldiers who died there by analysing satellite imagery and official photographs of a newly built memorial in Pyongyang.
The leaked Russian statistics may not be complete but taken in conjunction with BBC Russian's own work they are significant.
In the context of a war that has lasted four years and 10 months, these are high numbers for Russia, when compared with the Soviet war in Afghanistan that ended in 1989.
In that 10-year war, an estimated 15,000 Red Army troops died, and an estimated one million civilians were killed.

Domestic energy prices are set to soar in January under the regulator Ofgem's new price cap, pushing up bills for millions of households across England, Scotland and Wales.
With household budgets already under pressure, finding ways to reduce gas and electricity costs has become increasingly important. But how much difference can simple changes really make?
The BBC spoke to three people about what they're doing to keep their energy costs down.
Kelly Anne Harvey uses electric blankets and portable oil radiators in some rooms to save on the central heating
Like many people, Kelly Anne Harvey, a building surveyor from Cleveleys near Blackpool, is worried about her energy bill going up next year.
The 44-year-old, who is married with a five-year-old son, has a combined household income of £60,000.
She currently pays about £154 a month for gas and electricity on a standard variable rate with Octopus, but is looking for a fixed-rate deal to offset the rise.
The family fell into arrears on their energy bills a few years ago and Kelly says she won't let it happen again.
To control her costs she pays by direct debit, which spreads her payments and is typically £138 cheaper a year than paying on receipt of a bill .
The family uses electric blankets and portable oil radiators in some rooms so they don't have to turn the central heating on as often.
They also take part in Octopus's energy saving scheme, which rewards customers who use less electricity at peak times, such as early evenings, with a free hour of energy at the weekend.
"On Sunday we'll turn on the dishwasher, tumble drier, washing machine and maybe even charge our electric cars," says Kelly.
Stacey says she keeps the curtains closed "to keep the heat in" and her daughters wear thermal clothing
Stacey, 40, a single mother from Bristol, says dealing with rising energy costs has felt like a "battle" recently and she's worried about 2027.
The office worker, whose daughters are aged 10 and 12, is on a fixed-term tracker tariff with E.On Next, which charges rates set below the quarterly Ofgem price cap. She expects to pay £1,800 for energy this year, up £400 on last year.
Stacey, who is part of the Changing Realities project at Glasgow University, which documents life for people on low incomes, has tried a number of things to control her energy costs.
She's turned her central heating down from 22C to 19.5C, bought electric blankets and pays her bills by direct debit.
She also leaves her curtains shut to "keep the heat in", while her daughters wear thermal clothing if it gets chilly in the house. The family is also using less hot water.
"I've got girls and they're growing up and they want to spend loads of time in the shower [but] it's just not possible."
Around 1.5 million households in the UK rely on heating oil for heating and hot water, and their costs have already soared in the past year due to disruption in global oil markets.
"When I first moved here two years ago you could get a litre of heating oil for 50-60p," says Bradley Knowles, 32, who lives in a barn conversion with his husband, mother and sister in rural Lincolnshire.
"At the height of the Iran war it went up to £1.20 or £1.30 and now it's stabilised at around £1."
To cut costs, the finance worker orders oil in bulk, buying 1,000-1,500 litres, preferably in the summer months when prices are lower. He also tries to order a few weeks in advance to avoid expensive next-day deliveries.
Bradley uses comparison sites to see which local suppliers offer the cheapest oil and puts money aside each month so he can always afford his orders.
Oil-powered boilers may take time to heat up, but Bradley advises against leaving them on all day as that can be very expensive.
Instead, he uses an electric tank to store his warm water and tops up the heating in parts of the property with electric radiators.

Zeeshan Ali makes history as the first foreign national to board China’s space station
The first person from Pakistan to go into orbit has made history as the first foreign astronaut to board China’s Tiangong space station.
Muhammad Zeeshan Ali docked at the space station in the early hours of Wednesday after taking off from China’s Jiuquan Satellite Launch Centre in northwest China on board a Chinese-made rocket.
Ali, 40, will stay in space for five to 10 days, shorter than the usual six-month stints Chinese astronauts serve.
“I’m not flying for myself. I carry the name of Pakistan on my shoulder,” Ali told reporters on Tuesday.
While most of the infrastructure behind Ali’s space trip is Chinese, he has trained for months in China, including by learning Chinese, to make the trip happen.
“This is not just one astronaut’s journey, but the journey of 240 million Pakistanis. It is the journey of our younger generation, our scientists and our dreams,” Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif said in a post on X.
“This is living proof of the ironclad friendship between Pakistan and China. We are grateful to our brother country, China, for making Pakistan part of this historic mission.”
Chinese President Xi Jinping said the joint mission with astronauts from China and Pakistan is “a vivid embodiment of the deep-rooted friendship between the two countries”.
This is a big diplomatic moment for China. Beijing is eager to show the world that the Tiangong space station has the potential to become an international research platform rather than an exclusive Chinese facility.
China has been ramping up its space industry and aims to put a Chinese astronaut on the moon by 2030. The US aims to do the same in 2028, for the first time since the 1972 Apollo 17 flight.
China plans to establish a ‌research ‌base on the moon by 2035 with Russia.
Both Beijing and Washington insist their presence in space is entirely peaceful, but the US has warned that China could seek to dominate resource-rich areas of the moon.

Energy bills are to soar in January, as prices governed by regulator Ofgem's cap rise at the coldest time of the year.
The cap affects millions of people in England, Scotland and Wales, and reflects higher wholesale gas costs which have been pushed up by the US-Israel war with Iran.
It means people on variable tariffs should give an accurate meter reading, ensure they are receiving all the support to which they are entitled, and take care over energy use.
The energy cap fixes the maximum amount which customers on standard variable tariffs can be charged for each unit of gas and electricity used.
It covers more than 20 million households in England, Wales and Scotland and is set by the regulator Ofgem every three months , external .
It affects those paying by direct debit, by standard credit (they pay when they get a bill), or prepayment meters in slightly different ways.
Most of the increase in the energy price cap has, and will be, driven by higher gas prices.
The government's decision to temporarily remove VAT from domestic electricity bills has cut about £45 a year from a typical bill.
Meanwhile, millions of households will receive a £100 automatic payment to help cover winter costs.
The typical annual usage figure applies to the first category: dual-fuel households on a standard variable tariff which pay by direct debit.
But customers' actual bills depend on the amount of energy used and how they pay for it.
The roughly 11 million households on fixed tariffs do not see their prices change until the end of their fixed term.
Ofgem regulates the energy market in England, Scotland and Wales. Northern Ireland has a separate system.
Although the price cap sets the unit prices for gas and electricity, your household's actual bill depends on the overall amount of energy you use, and how you pay for it.
Where you live, the type of property you have, how energy efficient it is, how many people live there, and the weather all make a difference.
The Ofgem cap is illustrated using "typical" household energy use in a year with a single bill for gas and electricity settled by direct debit.
The vast majority of people pay their bill this way to help spread payments across the year.
In July, Ofgem reduced what it believes to be a "typical" level of energy use, because many homes have cut back due to high prices in recent years while energy efficiency has improved.
Its new estimate is 9,500 kWh of gas and 2,500 kWh of electricity a year.
Submitting a meter reading when the cap changes means you are not charged for estimated usage at the wrong rate.
Customers with working smart meters do not need to submit a reading as their bill is calculated automatically.
Ofgem also controls standing charges, which are a fixed daily fee to cover the costs of connecting households to gas and electricity supplies. These vary slightly by region , external and payment method.
Between 1 October and 31 December 2026, average standing charges for direct debit customers will be 54.83p a day for electricity and 29.68p a day for gas.
The electricity charge is lower than the amount charged in the previous three-month period, while the gas charge is largely unchanged.
Campaigners have long argued that standing charges are unfair because they make up a bigger proportion of the bill for low-energy households. Others say it just shifts the cost from one part of the bill to another rather than cutting it.
The government has announced plans to remove gas standing charges, although no details have been published on how that will happen
Fixed deals provide certainty for a set period – often a year, or longer – but if energy prices drop while you are on the deal, you could be stuck at a higher price.
You may also have to pay a penalty to leave a fixed deal early if you change your mind.
Experts recommend checking whole-of-market energy price comparison sites to help find the best deal and studying the details of exit fees.
Since 1 April, energy bill charges related to the low-income household insulation scheme - called the Energy Company Obligation - have been scrapped, and for three years, renewable energy projects will be 75%-funded by general taxation instead of a levy on energy bills.
Nearly everyone in England, Wales and Scotland will benefit from this cut, although the amounts will vary between households.
However, the cost of maintaining and strengthening energy network infrastructure like power lines, cables and gas pipes is rising.
In December 2025, Ofgem approved a £28bn investment to improve the electricity and gas grids in Great Britain to strengthen energy supplies and protect customers against volatile energy prices. It will also reduce Britain's dependence on gas.
Customers will pay part of the cost of the upgrade, through an additional £108 added to energy bills by 2031.
These charges started to appear from April 2026, adding about £6 a month to the bill for a typical household covered by the energy cap.
High electricity bills targeted in planned shakeup to energy pricing
Households could get free electricity for doing washing on sunny weekends
Suppliers must offer customers affordable payment plans or repayment holidays if they are struggling to pay their bills. Most also offer hardship grants.
Since the Russian invasion of Ukraine in 2022, bills have gone up by about 70% compared with the pre-crisis norm, and since then unpaid bills and charges have shot up.
Vanessa Northam, director at debt charity StepChange, has advice for people who may be struggling:
Look closely at how much energy you are using, and be alert to estimated bills, which might prove to be inaccurate
It is often best to try to talk to someone who can fully understand your situation
Heating oil is not covered by the energy cap. About 1.5 million UK households use heating oil and they have already seen a sharp increase in bills since the Middle East conflict triggered a jump in oil prices. Some users have seen costs more than double.
The issue is particularly acute in Northern Ireland, where about 500,000 homes use heating all, almost two-thirds of all households.
In March, the government announced a £53m support package to help low-income households in rural communities who use heating oil.

Ofgem’s price cap will increase for third quarter in a row after rise in wholesale cost of gas
Millions of British households will face annual energy bills of more than £2,000 a year for the first time since Russia’s invasion of Ukraine, as the cap on energy bills climbs for a third straight quarter.
Gas and electricity prices will rise by 26% from January under the government’s new price cap after an increase in wholesale prices not experienced since the first winter after the invasion.
The regulator for Great Britain, Ofgem , said about 22 million households covered by the price cap would need to pay an average equivalent to £2,166 a year for gas and electricity from the new year, up from £1,723 under the current quarterly cap.
The increase means that the average household will be forced to pay almost £600 a year more on their dual-fuel bill than before the start of the Middle East crisis. There was a 4% rise at the start of October and a 13% increase at the start of July.
About a third of households that pay for their gas and electricity on fixed tariffs will not be affected by the latest price cap rise. However, the highest energy price cap since early 2023 is still expected to reignite calls for the government to help struggling families and reduce reliance on fossil fuels.
The cap is a limit on how much energy suppliers can charge for a unit of electricity or gas, not a ceiling for how high bills can rise.
Miatta Fahnbulleh, the energy secretary, said: “I know people are deeply concerned by another rise in energy bills. For too long, British families have been paying the price for conflicts overseas and volatile fossil fuel markets.”
The government has promised to give “breathing space” to struggling households this winter through a one-off payment of £100 in January for 20 million households in council tax bands A to D.
The payment will be in addition to the warm home discount, which offers about 6 million means-tested households in England, Wales and Scotland £150 off winter fuel bills.
“But there is more to do to take the pressure off families and bring bills down for good,” Fahnbulleh said. “That means more cheap, clean, homegrown power so we’re less reliant on expensive fossil fuels, and reforming our broken energy system so it’s fairer for British people.”
The government help remains well below the surging prices for gas, electricity and road fuels, which have forced up living costs in the nine months since the US-Israeli strikes on Iran.
Energy bills are expected to only fall slightly in April, when the price cap is next set, according to a new forecast from Cornwall Insight on Wednesday. The energy consultancy said market volatility caused by disruption to the strait of Hormuz meant its predictions could change “several times” in the coming months.
Europe’s benchmark gas price has tripled in response to a global supply squeeze, that meant the continent entered the cooler months with gas stores at some of the lowest levels ever recorded .
The price could climb even higher, according to Goldman Sachs, if disruption to Gulf gas exports causes storage facilities to empty before the end of the heating season.
Craig Lowrey, a principal at Cornwall Insight, warned that if the Middle East conflict continues, current forecasts suggest bills could remain about £2,000 a year for the typical household until the end of 2027.
Lorwey said the forecast fall of 1% in April was “so small that many households will barely notice it, and by then the £100 payment, for those who are eligible, will be a distant memory”.
Ministers have sought to cushion the blow by moving electricity levies into general taxation over the past year, which has shaved about £150 a year off costs. The Treasury also promised to keep the 5% VAT levy off electricity bills for 29 million households until July next year, which should extend the tax relief to £50 a year.
Danny Gross, a climate campaigner at Friends of the Earth, called on the government to accelerate the shift to “cheap, homegrown renewable energy” to cushion energy bills from the volatility of the fossil fuel markets.
“This will cut bills, create long-term jobs, strengthen our energy security and tackle the climate crisis at the same time,” Gross said. “But people need relief now, not just promises. Ministers must introduce a social tariff to protect low-income households and move the hidden levies piled onto electricity bills into general taxation,” he added.

Suppliers said their own profits are also capped, and everyone was feeling the "impact of our exposure to volatile fossil fuel markets".
Energy UK, which represents suppliers, said the UK needed to develop more domestic clean power and accelerate the electrification of our homes and transport.
The increase is the largest seen since Russia's invasion of Ukraine drove up prices significantly. It comes at a tough time of year, when the weather is at its coldest and use is peaking.
Individual usage differs, so for every £100 spent on energy now, the new cost will be about £126.
The cap sets a maximum price for each unit of energy, not the total bill.

Gas will increase from 7.97p per kilowatt-hour to 10.96p, higher than in the wake of the invasion of Ukraine.

Failure to implement previous reports means institutional racism, misogyny and homophobia still present in force
Metropolitan police still institutionally racist and misogynist, says report
From the Stephen Lawrence inquiry in 1999 to Louise Casey’s landmark review in 2023, successive reports on the Metropolitan police have arrived at the same damning conclusion: Britain’s largest police force is institutionally racist.
It will, therefore, come as little surprise that three years after Casey’s report, an independent review led by Gillian Fairfield has found that institutional racism, misogyny and homophobia persist within the force.
But among the most striking findings of the Fairfield review is that the Met’s senior leadership appears to have become uncomfortable with even using the word “racism”.
During a series of strategic briefings in which senior officers outlined the progress made since Casey, the review noted that by the end of their third meeting, not a single senior leader had used the word racism. When pressed, officers and staff spoke instead of “disproportionality”.
Dal Babu, a former Met chief superintendent who sits on the London Policing Board, said this went to the heart of the problem: “Unless you acknowledge that you’ve got institutional racism, misogyny and homophobia, then your progress is always going to be extremely difficult.”
Babu said there had been progress on race but that it had been “glacial”. He pointed to the force’s firearms command as an example. “In 2007, they started an initiative to increase the number of women joining the firearms command,” he explained. “It was only when I raised it in 2025 that there was even an acknowledgment that there should be a similar scheme for Black officers.”
Beyond race, the review found that despite improvements in vetting and misconduct procedures, staff still feared retaliation for speaking up. As well as racism, the force treated misogyny and homophobia as a “reputational threat” rather than an opportunity for learning.
For Habib Kadiri, the executive director of the police monitoring organisation StopWatch, the proliferation of reports and recommendations has done little to inspire confidence that the force is prepared to confront the scale of the problem.
A Guardian investigation in May 2025 examined about 600 recommendations across 12 government-commissioned race reviews dating back to 1981. It found less than a third had been implemented in full. Politicians and commissioners warned at the time that the UK was stuck in a “doom loop” of reports followed by inaction.
“We’re frustrated that the good efforts of so many reports are wasted over generations, and that we are in a situation that’s really not very much better than it ever was,” Kadiri said. “And the solutions would require the police to have a lot more humility in the way that they police neighbourhoods that they would otherwise racialise.”
The review comes amid an increasingly polarised political debate about policing, in which attempts to address racial inequalities have been characterised by some on the right as evidence of preferential treatment or “two-tier policing”.
“They appear to be scared of using terms like ‘anti-racism’”, and that’s emboldened far-right-leaning organisations and supporters to critique the police from that angle,” Kadiri said.
He argued that the Met had retreated from an explicitly anti-racist stance in favour of the notion that treating everyone equally was sufficient to address racial inequality. In doing so, Kadiri said, the force continued to justify persistent racial disparities in stop and search by relying on what he regarded as flawed assumptions about Black people’s involvement in crime.
While there was notable criticism, the Fairfield review did recognise the considerable energy and investment that has gone into reform since 2023. The review also found that despite generations of strained relations between the Met and London’s Black communities, community groups continued to engage with the force.
“If I had my time over again, in the blink of an eye I’d join the police. And lots of people I know from the global majority, Black and Asian people, want to join the police,” Babu said.
“When I joined, I could count on one hand the number of people I worked with who didn’t use the P- and N-word. That would not happen now,” Babu said.
“I think the only way you are going to change things is that we get people to join from our communities and those people are valued.”

Students and stargazers packed SUPARCO’s auditorium before dawn to watch Zeeshan Ali reach orbit on a Chinese rocket.
Islamabad, Pakistan — It was 5:18am (00:18 GMT) on Wednesday, before dawn in a chilly Islamabad. On the screen at the front of the auditorium, a Chinese rocket carrying Muhammad Zeeshan Ali, Pakistan’s first astronaut, rose on a column of orange flames.
As the rocket lifted off, Pakistan’s national anthem began. The audience, which had been slouching in their seats, rose row by row and sang along.
While many took out their phones to record the historic moment, Zainab Abbasi’s eyes remained fixed on the giant screen.
“I had my phone out to record it on video, but I was so caught up in the moment that I forgot to record, and I was just standing there with my phone closed,” Abbasi, 21, told Al Jazeera.
A second-year undergraduate student of physics and astronomy at the National University of Sciences and Technology (NUST), Abbasi was with her friends in the auditorium at the headquarters of the Pakistan Space & Upper Atmosphere Research Commission (SUPARCO).
As the rocket climbed higher, the hall erupted in applause and chants of “Pakistan Zindabad” (“Long live Pakistan”).
The Long March-2F rocket lifted off from the Jiuquan Satellite Launch Centre in northwest China, carrying Chinese astronauts Tang Hongbo and Wu Yi, alongside Ali, a 40-year-old Pakistan Air Force pilot.
But within two minutes of liftoff, the hall fell silent. No one spoke. Faces across the rows were tense. On the screen, the rocket had shrunk to a dot.
“There was, I think, anticipation and also, for me specifically, a sort of, you know, underlying anxiety,” Abbasi told Al Jazeera.
On January 28, 1986, the US space shuttle Challenger broke apart 73 seconds after liftoff, killing all seven crew members.
About 10 minutes after Wednesday’s launch, the Shenzhou-24 spacecraft separated from the rocket and entered orbit, according to the China Manned Space Agency (CMSA).
The silence lasted several minutes, until one of the hosts congratulated the audience on a successful launch. People got up, greeted one another or headed for the doors.
A few hours later, CMSA and SUPARCO confirmed that the spacecraft had docked at China’s Tiangong space station at 8:56am (03:56 GMT). The crew were expected to enter the station at about 11:45am (06:45 GMT).
The auditorium had been packed by 5am (00:00 GMT). Those unable to find a seat sat on the floor or stood along the walls.
Tayyaba Riaz, a final-year mathematics student at NUST, said every seat was taken when she arrived at about 4:20am (23:20 GMT Tuesday). Originally from Chitral in Pakistan’s northwest, she lives in a university hostel.
When she asked hostel authorities to leave early in the morning, she said they asked where she was going. “I was like, ‘I am going to witness a history,’” she said, giggling.
Many in the auditorium held glossy cards bearing Ali’s portrait in a spacesuit and the words “Pakistan’s First Manned Space Mission”. Paper flags of Pakistan and China rested on laps, while green and white balloons lined the stage.
The screen carried a livestream of the launch. There was a brief moment of hilarity when, just before liftoff, a YouTube advertisement appeared, causing mild panic that the critical moment might be missed.
Abbasi, the second-year student, had been at SUPARCO since 2am (21:00 GMT Tuesday). She lives 40km (25 miles) away and had left home at 7pm (14:00 GMT) on Tuesday to spend the night at her aunt’s house nearby.
She is a member of PakAstronomers, a group of amateur astronomers in Islamabad. Her interest in astronomy began around 2018, when she was 13, after the cartoon series Beyblade introduced her to constellations.
Her family, particularly her father, has always supported her, even if they do not always understand her passion, she said.
“When I was a child and interested in space, becoming an astronaut felt like a far-off dream only available to a child in America and not in Pakistan,” she said.
Ahzam Farooq, a physics undergraduate at NUST and vice president of the society, used to wake at 3am to watch rocket launches.
“My parents used to ask, ‘What is there in this?’ like it will never be us,” he said.
Adan Athar, a second-year space sciences student at the Institute of Space Technology (IST) in Islamabad, is from Faisalabad and a founding member of the Faisalabad Astronomical Society.
She told Al Jazeera she was the first in her family to take an interest in space.
“Yes, they were very supportive, and they think I will be the next astronaut,” she said with a shy smile.
But it is not only Pakistan’s youth following Ali’s journey.
Saif-ul-Islam Qureshi, a 72-year-old electronics engineer, has been watching the sky for at least 50 years.
“I was 12 years old when I started this hobby with my small binocular, and then my first observation was the Big Dipper in the sky,” he told Al Jazeera.
The Big Dipper is a group of seven bright stars whose two end stars point towards the North Star.
Qureshi helped found PakAstronomers, the group Abbasi belongs to. It was initially called the Pakistan Astronomy Society.
Its members took astronomy to schools, colleges, universities and public parks. Many people did not know planets could be seen with the naked eye, he said.
Over the past decade, however, that had changed. Even small children were now well informed.
“We were sensing that a storm was building. A storm is building, and a storm in a positive sense,” he said.
In a speech before the launch, SUPARCO chairman Muhammad Yousaf Khan said Pakistan was setting its sights further ahead.
“Our ambition is beyond just this launch. Our commitment is to reach the moon by 2035,” he said.
Speaking to Al Jazeera afterwards, Khan said the first step would be a lunar rover, due to fly in 2028.
“If the Chinese people have reached here, there is no shortcoming in us. I believe one day, we too will reach that stage, if we keep moving step by step,” Khan told Al Jazeera.
Farooq, the NUST physics undergraduate, said collaboration with China could help Pakistan avoid having to build its space capabilities from scratch.
“If we have this collaboration, I think it’s good that we can use the already built-up platforms of China and utilise them to do something further. By making our own satellites, and through our own astronauts, we can go towards some further research,” he told Al Jazeera.
For Qureishi, the veteran astronomer, that excitement for the future climaxed when Ali took off. That moment, he said, was about much more than Ali.
“It is not Zeeshan [in the astronaut’s seat]. It is Pakistan’s young generation sitting there,” he said.

Thomas Markle, the father of Meghan, Duchess of Sussex has been charged by a federal grand jury in Los Angeles with possessing child sex abuse images.
Markle, who remains in custody in Florida, allegedly possessed materials that include at least one image involving a prepubescent minor and a minor under 12 years old, court documents filed in California show.
The 82-year-old has denied possessing images of child sex abuse.
Last week, a judge in Florida declared Prince Harry's father-in-law mentally competent to stand trial.
The FBI arrested Markle on 6 November at an elderly care home in Florida on a single federal charge of possessing child sexual abuse material. He now faces two counts.
US attorney Bill Essayli said Markle faces a maximum of 20 years in prison on each count if convicted.
His arrest came after a search of a storage unit he had allegedly rented in Los Angeles for almost two decades uncovered the abuse material.
Markle was initially released on conditional bail but was then ordered to stay in jail pending trial after allegedly removing a location monitoring device.
Watch: Thomas Markle's charges over child sexual abuse material
In the indictment, filed by the US Attorney's Office in the Central District of California, Markle is accused of knowingly possessing 35mm film negatives on 30 October and 4 November that contained child sexual abuse materials.
The US Attorney's Office said that during both instances Markle allegedly knew the images contained such materials.
Inside the storage units, federal agents found two images that depict an adult man - whom a witness identified as Markle - with an underage child, the US attorney's office said.
They also alleged that a third image appears to depict a child in a room believed to be part of a motel chain in the Philippines. Markle moved to the Philippines last year after he had a series of strokes, and he lived in Cebu until May.
"The affidavit also describes additional photographs that appear to show Markle with children in various stages of undress," prosecutors said.

FILE - Senegal's Sadio Mane holds the trophy aloft as he celebrates with teammates after winning the Africa Cup of Nations final soccer match between Senegal and Morocco in Rabat, Morocco, Sunday, Jan. 18, 2026. Youssef Loulidi/AP hide caption
More than 10 months on from a chaotic, controversial final, Senegal is Africa's soccer champion once again.
Senegal won back the Africa Cup of Nations title in a legal fight on Tuesday after the Court of Arbitration for Sport overturned an earlier ruling which handed the trophy to Morocco.
Senegal won the Africa Cup on the field in Morocco in January and then lost it in a legal case in March because its players walked off the field in protest in second-half stoppage time.
CAS has now rejected that earlier ruling, based on referee Jean-Jacques Ndala's decision to let the game resume after the protest.
"The Court of Arbitration for Sport has delivered justice to sport," Senegalese soccer federation president Abdoulaye Fall said in a statement.
The legal battle may not be over yet after Morocco announced plans to appeal, likely to Switzerland's supreme court, in a challenge to the integrity of a senior CAS judge.
Tournament regulations said a team which refuses to play should be considered to have lost the game, but CAS said those rules were meant only for cases "when a team's conduct leads the referee to call off the game permanently."
Ndala "did not err in law" when he resumed the game and had "sole authority" to make that call, CAS said, adding its three judges were unanimous.
"The panel acknowledged that the referee had to make a decision in an atmosphere of extreme tension," CAS said. "However, these circumstances do not justify describing the decision as 'arbitrary.' On the contrary, the referee's judgment did not appear to have been affected by factors external to the game."
Morocco's soccer federation detailed plans for an appeal that targets one of the three judges on the CAS panel.
In a statement, the Moroccan federation protested what it described as the court's failure to address potential integrity concerns, alleging "confirmed communication" between German arbitrator Ulrich Haas and Fall, the Senegalese soccer president, 48 hours before the decision was issued.
The CAS director general, Matthieu Reeb, acknowledged to reporters at the court in Lausanne that a Moroccan protest was received just minutes before the verdict was announced.
Reeb said the court's panel "in charge of petitions for challenge has conceded that there was not enough elements at this stage to postpone the notification of the award."
CAS verdicts can be challenged at Switzerland's supreme court, also in Lausanne, though only on limited procedural grounds of which a judge's integrity could be one.
Haas has been among the most respected and in-demand CAS judges in the past 20 years, selected by parties in storied cases involving Manchester City's beating a Champions League ban by UEFA, tennis star Simona Halep's doping case and Africa's Champions League final in 2019.
Patrick Kabou, a lawyer for the Senegalese Soccer Federation, called the alleged communication between Fall and Haas "unreal."
Senegal won the final 1-0 after extra time with chaos on the field and violent clashes in the stands. Even the ball boys were involved in scuffles as they tried to snatch towels that Senegal goalkeeper Edouard Mendy was using to keep his gloves dry.
The result was overturned two months later as a 3-0 default win for Morocco by an appeals panel appointed by the Confederation of African Football (CAF).
Senegal beat AFCON host nation Morocco after a 15-minute delay in play. At 0-0, Senegal's team walked off the field to protest Morocco being awarded a penalty kick in the last minute of regulation time.
Match referee Ndala of Congo eventually allowed the game to restart, Morocco's penalty by Real Madrid forward Brahim Diaz — a slow chip shot known as a "Panenka" — was saved, and Senegal won in extra time.
The drama continued through the months of legal tussles. Senegal's players paraded with the trophy ahead of a game in March against Peru, even though Morocco was recognized as the champion at that point.
Both teams played at the World Cup believing themselves to be the rightful champion of Africa.
Senegal had the laws of the game on its side, and Morocco had the tournament regulations.
The laws of soccer state that referee decisions are final. CAS backed that position with its own "field of play" doctrine, that on-field calls by a referee generally can't be taken to the sports court.
"By blowing his whistle to restart play, the referee considered that the conditions for resuming the match had been met — both teams were on the pitch again, and both expressed their willingness to resume," CAS said.
In the first legal case in March, CAF appeal judges cited AFCON tournament regulations that if a team "refuses to play or leaves the ground before the regular end of the match without the authorization of the referee, it shall be considered loser and shall be eliminated for good from the current competition."
The CAS judges heard evidence at a one-day hearing last month and the court promised a verdict by the end of November with a full written ruling of its judges setting out reasons for their decision.
The next men's AFCON starts in June co-hosted by Kenya, Uganda, and Tanzania. Morocco will aim to end a wait for the title which now stands at 50 years.
"Senegal won on the pitch, and the court simply confirmed what we all already knew: We are the real champions of Africa," said Mariama Sidibé, 35, an accountant in the capital, Dakar.
Sidibé said the dispute between Morocco and Senegal should now be left in the past.
"With all of this behind us, we should focus on what unites us now, and who knows, maybe Morocco can have its revenge on the field during the next AFCON this summer," she said.
"At the end of the day Morocco and Senegal are brothers," Sidibé added, referring to the countries' long shared close ties built on religion, trade and culture.
Sidi Sylla, a philosophy student at Dakar's main university, said the court's ruling was "not just a win for Senegal but for football in general."
CAS rulings have stripped many athletes of Olympic medals for doping, but it's rare to overturn the result of a major soccer competition.
CAS refused to change the results of the 2019 Asian Cup, dismissing an appeal that the star striker on winning team Qatar shouldn't have been eligible for the tournament.
A lengthy legal battle over the same year's African Champions League final also ended with the original winner, Esperance of Tunisia, taking the title after its opponent Wydad from Morocco refused to play on.
One notable CAS ruling on a team sport title came at the Winter Olympics in 2022. A doping case involving then-15-year-old Russian figure skater Kamila Valieva ended up with her disqualification, and the Russian team being dropped from gold to bronze in the team event.

Porto Riko'dan Jennifer Barreto, 2026 Kainat Güzeli (Miss Universe) seçildi. Barreto, tacını geçen yılın kraliçesi Meksikalı Fatima Bosch'un elinden aldı.
27 yaşındaki sosyal hizmet uzmanı, ABD'nin özerk bölgesi olan Porto Riko'nun başkenti San Juan'da düzenlenen büyük finalde, vize sorunları ve çekişmeli bir iş anlaşmazlığı nedeniyle son dakika çekilmeleriyle sayısı önemli ölçüde azalan 115 finalist arasından zafer kazandı.
Barreto, organizatörlerin üç yıl önce evlenmiş veya doğum yapmış yarışmacılara yönelik tartışmalı yasağını kaldırmasından bu yana Kainat Güzellik Yarışması'nı kazanan ilk evli ve çocuklu kadın oldu.
Latin Amerikalı yarışmacılar için başarılı geçen yarışmada, Dominik Cumhuriyeti'nden Melissa Nunez ikinci, Venezuela'dan Clara Vegas da üçüncü oldu.
Final gecesi, çeşitli ön eleme yarışmalarından alınan jüri puanlarına dayalı bir eleme turuyla başladı. Kalan 30 yarışmacı daha sonra sahne üzerinde bir mayo geçidine katıldı ve 12'si gece elbisesi geçit törenine yükseldi. Son beş yarışmacı daha sonra, Miss Universe yarışmasının önemi ve dünyanın liderlerinden neye ihtiyacı olduğu gibi konular üzerine jüri sorularıyla karşı karşıya kaldı.
Yapay zekanın gelişmesi karşısında "asla kaybetmememiz gereken" insani değerin hangisi olduğu sorulduğunda, Barreto "En iyisi onu sorumlu bir şekilde kullanmaktır. Eğer yapay zeka değerlerimizi tehlikeye atıyorsa, o zaman bunlar hiçbir zaman değer olmamıştır. Değerler, özellikle bu şeyleri korumak zorlaştığında, söylediklerimizle yaptıklarımız arasındaki tutarlılıkta bulunur" dedi.
Türkiye'yi Kainat Güzellik Yarışması sahnesinde temsil eden son isim 2025 yılında Ceren Arslan oldu. 2026 sürecinde ise Alara Eriç'in katılımı uçuş günü iptal edildi. Eriç, pasaportu ve ABD vizesiyle uçuş için hazır beklediği sabah organizasyonun kendisine "eksiklerin giderilmediği ve hazır olmadığı" gerekçesiyle katılımının iptal edildiğini bildirdiğini açıkladı. Bu süreçte üniversitede üç dersini ertelediğini ve bursunun yandığını belirtti.
Miss Universe Türkiye Organizasyonu, kararın sorumluluğunu üstlendiğini duyurdu. Gerekçe olarak Eriç'in 4 Kasım'daki son sınavından sonraki hazırlık çalışmalarına düzenli katılmamasını, son kıyafet provalarında yer almamasını ve tanıtım videosu için istenen 30 saniyelik seslendirmeyi tamamlamamasını gösterdi.
Görkemli final sorunsuz geçerken, bu yılki tartışmaların çoğu etkinliğe giden haftalar ve aylarda ortaya çıktı.
Nepal ve Güney Sudan ile Kongo Cumhuriyeti'nin de aralarında bulunduğu beş Afrika ülkesinden güzellik kraliçeleri, ABD vizesi alma zorlukları veya gecikmeleri nedeniyle yarışmadan çekilmek zorunda kaldı. Öte yandan, Miss Universe Organizasyonu ile altı Güneydoğu Asya ülkesinde eleme yarışmaları düzenleyen Taylandlı iş insanı Nawat Itsaragrisil arasında devam eden bir sözleşme anlaşmazlığı nedeniyle Endonezya, Laos, Malezya, Singapur, Tayland ve Vietnam'dan gelen yarışmacılar finalde yer alamadı.
Daha önce mayıs ayında, Miss Universe Fransa organizatörleri, oylamada hile ve kayırmacılık iddialarına karışan 2025 finaline protesto amacıyla temsilcilerini geri çekmişti.
Geçen yıl, finalden üç gün önce, jüri üyesi Omar Harfouch, sonuçların resmi olmayan bir jüri tarafından önceden belirlendiğine inandığı için istifa etmişti. Harfouch ayrıca, geçen yıl tacı alan Meksika Güzeli Fatima Bosch'un, babasının Miss Universe'ün ortak sahibi Raul Rocha Cantu ile olduğu iddia edilen iş bağlantıları nedeniyle kazandığını öne sürmüştü.
Tartışmalı Meksikalı iş insanı ve Miss Universe Organizasyonu, iddiaları sürekli olarak reddetti. Ancak jüri üyelerinin finalden sadece bir gün önce açıklanmasıyla, bu yılki yarışmanın değerlendirme süreciyle ilgili sorular gündeme geldi.
Porto Riko, bu yılki birincisiyle birlikte altı kez Kainat Güzeli çıkarmış oldu. ABD özerk toprağı olan Porto Riko, yarışmanın 75 yıllık tarihinde dördüncü kez finale ev sahipliği yaptı. Daha önce 1972, 2001 ve 2002 yıllarında da finale ev sahipliği yapmıştı.
Miss Universe organizasyonu, yarışmanın modernleşmesi yönündeki artan çağrılar ışığında, hamile kadınlar, anneler, evli olan veya daha önce evlenmiş olan yarışmacılar üzerindeki tartışmalı yasağı kaldırdı. 2023 yılında organizatörler ayrıca 28 yaş üstü yasağını da sona erdirdi.
Final öncesi düzenlenen kostüm yarışması sırasında, İsrail Güzeli Danielle Yablonka, üzerinde İngilizce, İbranice ve Arapça olarak "barış" yazan bir pelerinle podyumda yürürken yuhalama sesleri duyuldu. Bu tasarım, İsrail'in Gazze'deki saldırılarının devam ettiği bir dönemde tepkilere yol açtı.
Resmi Miss Israel Instagram hesabı, kostüm konsepti açıklarken, "barış" kelimesinin diller arası ortak bir umut mesajı olduğunu belirtti.
Danielle Yablonka, ulusal kostüm bölümünde yuhalandığını gösteren ve internette dolaşan videolarla ilgili demecinde, kendisinin herhangi bir yuhalama duymadığını ve sesin videolara sonradan eklenmiş olabileceğini öne sürdü.
Times of Israel'in haberine göre İsrail Güzeli, "Yuhalamaların videoya sonradan eklenmiş olduğundan yüzde 99 eminim. Gerçek hayatta kimse yuhalamaları duymadı" dedi.
Yablonka ayrıca, "Yuhalasalar bile devam ederdim çünkü çok fazla adrenalinim vardı ve sanki tüm insanları omuzlarımda taşıyormuş gibi hissediyordum" ifadesini kullandı.

The United Nations condemned as "abhorrent" the flogging of Iranian singer Parastoo Ahmadi and four members of her production team, urging Tehran to abolish the practice. The five received 74 lashes each on Monday following a performance viewed millions of times on YouTube, local media reported, citing Ahmadi's lawyer.
The United Nations branded the lashing of a prominent Iranian singer and her production team as "abhorrent" and said Tehran must eradicate flogging.
Parastoo Ahmadi and four members of her team were lashed 74 times each on Monday after a performance viewed millions of times on YouTube , according to local media reports citing her lawyer.
All the musicians wore black, with Ahmadi dressed in a long, strappy gown and wearing deep red lipstick, in a country where women are banned from singing in public. They are also required to dress modestly and wear the headscarf .
Read more Iran's courts order US to pay $290 billion in damages
Ahmadi, 29, was sentenced in June to the lashes alongside the others, for the concert posted online in December 2024.
"The flogging of Iranian singer Parastoo Ahmadi and four male members of her team – following a concert she gave without wearing headcover – is abhorrent," UN rights chief Volker Turk said on X.
"Flogging is a form of torture or other cruel, inhuman or degrading punishment, absolutely prohibited under international law in all circumstances.
"Iran must abstain from carrying out other flogging sentences and eradicate this practice from its laws."
Increasing numbers of Iranian women are appearing without hijab, especially since protests erupted following the death in custody of a woman named Mahsa Amini in September 2022. She had been arrested for allegedly violating the dress code.

Topluluklara yönelik görevlerde çalışan Barreto, 24 Kasım Salı gecesi ev sahibi seyircinin önünde kainat güzeli ilan edildi. Tacı bir önceki kazanan, Meksikalı Fatima Bosch'tan devralan genç kadın, 115 rakibini geride bırakarak Porto Rico'ya ülkenin altıncı Miss Universe unvanını getirdi. Final gecesinin soru turunda yapay zekânın etkisi ve toplumun korunması gereken insani değerler soruldu; Barreto, yapay zekânın kalıcı olduğunu ve dikkatli kullanılması gerektiğini söylerken, liderlik sorusunda topluluğun ihtiyaçlarını dinlemenin ve olumlu örnek olmanın önemine değindi. Yarışmada ikinciliği Dominik Cumhuriyeti'nden Melissa Nunez, üçüncülüğü ise Venezuela'dan Clara Vegas aldı. Barreto'nun tacıyla sonuçlanan bu finale, sahneye çıkamayan ülkelerin hikâyesi de eşlik etti.
Finalde yer alamayan ülkelerin gerekçeleri birbirinden farklıydı. Habertürk 'ün aktardığına göre beş Afrika ülkesinin yarışmacısı vize güçlükleri nedeniyle yarıştan çekilirken, Endonezya, Laos, Malezya, Singapur, Tayland ve Vietnam yarışmacıları Miss Universe ile Taylandlı iş insanı Nawat Itsaragrisil arasındaki sözleşme anlaşmazlığı yüzünden finalde yer almadı. Türkiye'yi temsil edecek olan Alara Eriç ise pasaportu ve ABD vizesiyle hazır beklerken, uçuş günü organizasyonun eksiklerin giderilmediği ve hazır olmadığı gerekçesiyle katılımını iptal ettiğini açıkladı. Miss Universe Türkiye Organizasyonu kararın sorumluluğunu üstlenerek Eriç'in 4 Kasım'daki son sınavdan sonra hazırlıklara düzenli katılmadığını, son kıyafet provalarında bulunmadığını ve 30 saniyelik tanıtım seslendirmesini tamamlamadığını öne sürdü. Bu nedenle Türkiye, 75. Miss Universe finalinde temsil edilemedi.

UEFA Şampiyonlar Ligi 'nin 5. haftasında Real Madrid ile PSV Eindhoven karşı karşıya geldi. Maça ilk 11'de başlayan milli futbolcumuz Arda Güler , PSV'nin öne geçtiği gecede ikinci yarının başrol oyuncularından biri oldu. 21 yaşındaki yıldız 70. dakikada oyundan alınırken Bernabeu tribünleri onu ayakta alkışladı.
PSV, Tchouameni'nin ceza sahasındaki faulünün VAR incelemesiyle penaltıya dönmesinin ardından 32. dakikada Ivan Perisic'le öne geçti ve devreyi 1-0 önde kapattı. İkinci yarı başlar başlamaz ceza sahasında Diomande'nin pasıyla buluşan Arda Güler , Valverde'nin koşusunu görüp topu topuğuyla bıraktı, Uruguaylı oyuncu da 50. dakikada skoru eşitledi. İki dakika sonra gole kendisi de çok yaklaşan milli futbolcunun şutunu kaleci Kovar ayağıyla çıkardı. 64. dakikada rakip yarı alanda topu kapıp ceza sahasına giren Arda bu kez Mbappe'yi gördü, Fransız yıldız da durumu 3-1'e getirdi. Bu iki pasla Arda'nın bu sezonki asist sayısı 8'e yükselirken milli oyuncu Şampiyonlar Ligi 'nde 1 gol ve 4 asiste, La Liga'da ise 3 gol ve 4 asiste ulaştı.
Maça yedek kulübesinde başlayıp sonradan oyuna giren Jude Bellingham, 60. dakikada topu sol ayağıyla kaldırıp sağ ayağıyla havada kontrol ettikten sonra ayağının dışıyla vurdu ve Real Madrid'i 2-1 öne geçirdi. İngiliz yıldız, Vinicius Junior'ın attığı beşinci golün de asistini yaptı. Maçın ardından Real Madrid TV'ye konuşan Bellingham şu ifadeleri kullandı:
'İlk yarı sert ve zorlu geçti. Karşımızda çok kaliteli bir takım vardı ama ikinci yarıda bizim seviyemiz çok daha yüksekti. Basit işleri daha iyi yaptığımız için daha iyi oynadık. İnsanlar harika şeyler yapan kaliteli oyuncularımız olduğunu biliyor ancak bazen basit şeyleri iyi yapmak daha önemli.'
70. dakikada yerini Eduardo Camavinga'ya bırakan Arda Güler , tribünlerin ayakta alkışları arasında kenara geldikten sonra takım arkadaşları, teknik heyet ve güvenlik görevlileriyle tek tek tokalaştı. Bu sezon Şampiyonlar Ligi 'nde oynadığı her maçta gol atan Mbappe, 84. dakikada Brahim Diaz'ın pasında kaleci Kovar'ı geçerek ikinci golünü kaydetti. 87. dakikada Vinicius Junior'ın golüyle maç 5-1 sona erdi. Puanını 15'e yükselten Real Madrid resmi maçlardaki galibiyet serisini 10'a çıkarırken PSV 4 puanda kaldı. İspanyol ekibi Devler Ligi'ndeki bir sonraki maçında Arsenal deplasmanına gidecek, PSV ise Atletico Madrid'i ağırlayacak.
Real Madrid Teknik Direktörü Jose Mourinho, maç sonu basın toplantısında ilk yarıyı çok kötü bulduğunu söylerken devre arasında oyuncularına hatalarını üç görüntü üzerinden gösterdiklerini anlattı. Portekizli teknik adam, ikinci yarıdaki değişimi değerlendirirken şu ifadeleri kullandı:
'Beş numara takıma bambaşka bir dinamizm kazandırdı. Bence stoperleri değiştirmekten daha çok etki eden şey, orta sahada Bernardo ve Arda ile oynamamızdı. Onlar sadece futbol oynamayı bilen iki oyuncu. Savunmacı ya da pozisyonunu bekleyen oyuncular değiller ve maça farklı bir dinamizm verdik.'

Porto Riko'nun başkenti San Juan'da düzenlenen 75. Kainat Güzellik Yarışması'nın (Miss Universe 2026) kazananı belli oldu. 24 Kasım'da gerçekleştirilen finalde Porto Riko'yu temsil eden Jennifer Barreto, 2026 Kainat Güzeli seçildi.
27 yaşındaki Barreto, tacını 2025 Kainat Güzeli Meksikalı Fátima Bosch'un elinden aldı.
Bu sonuçla Porto Riko, Miss Universe tarihinde altıncı kez birincilik elde etti. Yarışmada Dominik Cumhuriyeti'nden Melissa Núñez ikinci, Venezuela'dan Clara Vegas ise üçüncü sırada yer aldı.
Sosyal hizmet uzmanı Jennifer Barreto, Miss Universe tarihinde bir ilke imza attı.
Yarışmanın evli kadınların ve annelerin katılımına izin veren düzenlemesinin ardından Barreto, hem evli hem de çocuk sahibi olarak Kainat Güzeli seçilen ilk yarışmacı oldu.
Organizasyon, daha önce evli kadınların ve annelerin yarışmaya katılmasını engelleyen kurallarını değiştirmişti. Ayrıca yarışmacılar için uygulanan 28 yaş sınırı da kaldırılmıştı.
Finalde yarışmacılara güncel toplumsal konulara ilişkin sorular yöneltildi. Yapay zekânın gelişmesi karşısında insanların kaybetmemesi gereken değerlerin sorulduğu Barreto, teknolojinin sorumlu kullanılması gerektiğini vurguladı.
Miss Universe 2026 öncesinde Türkiye temsilcisi Alara Eriç'in yarışmaya katılımının iptal edilmesi de tartışma yarattı.
Türkiye'yi temsil etmek üzere seçilen Eriç, Porto Riko'ya hareket edeceği gün organizasyon tarafından katılımının iptal edildiğini açıkladı.
Pasaportu ve ABD vizesiyle yolculuğa hazır olduğunu belirten Eriç, hazırlık sürecinde üniversitedeki üç dersini ertelediğini ve bursunu kaybettiğini söyledi.
Miss Universe Türkiye Organizasyonu ise iptal kararının sorumluluğunu üstlendi.
Organizasyon, Eriç'in 4 Kasım'daki son sınavının ardından yürütülen hazırlık çalışmalarına düzenli katılmadığını, kıyafet provalarında bulunmadığını ve tanıtım videosu için istenen seslendirmeyi tamamlamadığını öne sürdü.
Eriç'in katılımının iptal edilmesi nedeniyle Türkiye, 2026 Kainat Güzellik Yarışması'nın finalinde temsil edilmedi.
Yarışmanın ulusal kostüm bölümünde İsrail'i temsil eden Danielle Yablonka'nın sahneye çıkışı da tartışmalara neden oldu.
Yablonka, üzerinde İngilizce, İbranice ve Arapça olarak "barış" yazan bir pelerinle podyumda yürüdü.
İsrail'in Gazze'ye yönelik saldırılarının sürdüğü dönemde kullanılan kostüm, sosyal medyada eleştirilere neden oldu.
Yarışmacının podyumda yürüdüğü sırada yuhalandığını öne süren görüntüler de sosyal medyada yayıldı.
Yablonka ise bu iddialara karşı çıkarak sahnede herhangi bir yuhalama duymadığını söyledi. İsrailli yarışmacı, görüntülerdeki seslerin sonradan eklenmiş olabileceğini savundu.
Miss Universe 2026, final öncesinde yaşanan katılım sorunlarıyla da gündeme geldi.
Bazı ülkelerin temsilcileri ABD vizesi almakta yaşadıkları güçlükler nedeniyle yarışmaya katılamadı.
Öte yandan Miss Universe Organizasyonu ile Taylandlı iş insanı Nawat Itsaragrisil arasındaki yetki ve sözleşme anlaşmazlığı nedeniyle Endonezya, Laos, Malezya, Singapur, Tayland ve Vietnam'dan yarışmacılar finalde yer almadı.
Yarışma organizasyonunun yönetimi ve değerlendirme süreçlerine ilişkin tartışmalar da önceki yıllarda olduğu gibi bu yıl gündeme geldi.
Tüm tartışmaların gölgesinde düzenlenen finalin ardından 2026 Kainat Güzeli seçilen Jennifer Barreto, Porto Riko'ya yarışma tarihindeki altıncı birinciliğini kazandırdı.

MasterChef Türkiye ile tanınan ve bir dönem 7 milyon liralık villasıyla konuşulan Güzide Mertcan, uzun süren sessizliğini bu kez bir roman haberiyle bozdu. Yayınevinde sözleşme imzaladığı anların fotoğraflarını paylaşan Mertcan'ın aşk ve dramı bir araya getiren bir kitap yazdığı öğrenildi, sosyal medyada ilk tepki ise şaşkınlık oldu.
MasterChef Türkiye 'nin 2019 sezonuna katılan Güzide Mertcan, yarışmada üst sıralara kadar yükselmiş ve izleyicinin yakından tanıdığı isimler arasına girmişti. Programdan önce moda ve tekstil sektöründe çalışan Mertcan, yarışmanın ardından sosyal medya hesaplarıyla da takip edilen bir isim hâline geldi. Yaşadığı ev, paylaştığı hayat kareleri ve verdiği röportajlar yarışmanın ardından magazin gündeminde sık sık yer buldu. Bu ilginin en büyük kısmını da yarışmadan kısa süre sonra gündeme oturan villa haberleri çekti.
Mertcan'ın yaşadığı 10 odalı villa, yanındaki helikopter pistiyle birlikte 7 milyon liralık değeri üzerinden haberlere konu olmuş, evin aylık aidatının bile 3 bin 500 lira olduğu yazılmıştı. Aralık 2019'da evin satışa çıkarıldığı iddia edilirken Mertcan, Ocak 2020'de kendi YouTube kanalından villayı sattıklarını duyurdu. O günlerde evde yaklaşık dört buçuk yıldır oturduklarını anlatan Mertcan, 10 yıllık evliliği boyunca altı kez ev taşıdığını da söylemişti. Aynı dönemde kendi restoranını açmaya hazırlandığı haberlere yansıyan Mertcan'ın, bugünkü haberde de Gaziosmanpaşa'daki restoranını işletmeye devam ettiği belirtiliyor. Restoran işletmeciliğiyle anılan Mertcan'dan bu kez beklenmedik bir alandan haber geldi.
Mertcan'ın paylaştığı fotoğraflar, aşk ve dramı harmanlayan bir roman yazdığını ve bunun için yayınevinde sözleşme imzaladığını gösterdi. Kitabın adı, yayınevi ve çıkış tarihi henüz açıklanmadı. Paylaşımı görenlerin bir kısmı haberi önce şaka sandığını yazarken, birçok kullanıcı 'Hayırlı olsun' diyerek tebrik mesajı bıraktı. Sosyal medyada 'Sonuna kadar şaka sandım' ve '10 parmağında 10 marifet' gibi yorumlar da öne çıktı. Mertcan'ın kitapla ilgili detayları ne zaman paylaşacağı ise henüz belli değil.

1 Eylül'de "Vira bismillah" diyerek denize açılan balıkçılar, sezonun geride kalan bölümünde tonlarca palamut avladı. Türkiye'nin önemli balıkçılık kentlerinden Sinop'ta da yoğun şekilde avlanan palamut, balıkçıların yüzünü güldürmeyi sürdürüyor .
Son yılların en bereketli palamut sezonunun yaşandığını belirten balıkçılar, Karadeniz'de palamut avcılığının bir süre daha devam edeceğini öngörüyor.
Sinop Merkez Su Ürünleri Kooperatifi Başkanı Namık Ünlü, Karadeniz'de son 80 yılın en bereketli palamut sezonunu yaşadıklarını söyledi.
Daha önce böyle bir tabloyla karşılaşmadıklarını anlatan Ünlü, "80 yılın bir bolluğu yaşanıyor. Daha önce hiç böyle bir şey görülmemiş Karadeniz'de. Balık ikinci, üçüncü kez çark ediyor. Boğazdan çıkacak zannettik, İğneada'dan balık tekrar geriye gelerek şu an doğuya gidiyor. Yani Karadeniz'in yerli balığı gibi oldu." dedi.
Ünlü, 2005 yılında da palamut avcılığının çok yoğun yapıldığını ancak bu sezonki bolluğu daha önce yaşamadıklarını belirterek, şöyle devam etti:
"2005 yılında oldu ara ara ama şöyle söyleyeyim bunun onda ikisi kadar. Yani bu bolluk ilk defa. Kasa bulamadık, sele bulamadık, buz yetişmedi, nakliyeci yetişmedi. Ekonomik yönden de çok uygun. Halkımız 50 liraya, 40 liraya bir kiloluk balık yiyor. Şimdi 10 tane balık 10 kilo geliyor ve 500 lira. Dolduruyor dolabına, yaza hazırlık yapıyor. Satışlardan da belli uygun olduğu zaman bayağı bir hareketlilik oluyor. Yani vatandaş bu sene uygun palamut yedi, halen de yemeye devam ediyor aynı şekilde."
Palamudun bol olmasının vatandaş açısından çok iyi olduğunu, buna karşın balıkçılar olarak arz fazlalığından ötürü zaman zaman sıkıntılar yaşadıklarını anlatan Ünlü, "Palamudun bolluğu halkımıza yaradı, bol bol ucuz balık yediler, yemeye de devam ediyorlar. Bundan da memnunuz." ifadesini kullandı.

Araç muayenesinde yaklaşık 20 yıldır süren TÜVTÜRK dönemi 15 Ağustos 2027'de kapanıyor, yerini TURKA markası alıyor. Ulaştırma ve Altyapı Bakanı Abdulkadir Uraloğlu, TBMM Plan ve Bütçe Komisyonu'nda 2027 bütçesini anlatırken yeni nesil sistemin Ağustos 2027'de devreye gireceğini ve kredi kartıyla ödemelerde komisyon alınmayacağını duyurdu. Yapay zekâ destekli muayene hatları ve artan istasyon sayısıyla bekleme sürelerinin kısalması hedefleniyor.
Uraloğlu, Bakanlığın 2027 bütçesini sunduğu toplantıda yeni nesil araç muayene sisteminin Ağustos 2027'de başlayacağını söyledi. Sistemin yapay zekâ desteğiyle muayenelerde güvenilirliği artıracağını, istasyonlardaki bekleme sürelerini ise kısaltacağını bildirdi. Aynı sunumda hızlı tren , 5G ve Kalkınma Yolu projelerine dair hedefler de paylaşıldı.
Geçişin arkasında bir sözleşme takvimi var. Araç muayene hizmetleri 2004'teki ihaleyle kuzey ve güney bölgeleri olarak özelleştirilmiş, imtiyaz sözleşmeleri 15 Ağustos 2007'de imzalanmıştı. Mevcut sözleşmeler 14 Ağustos 2027'de sona eriyor. 30 Temmuz 2026'da Ankara 'da düzenlenen törenle, ihaleyi kazanan MOI OGG ortaklığının kurduğu TURKA ile 2027-2047 dönemini kapsayan yeni imtiyaz sözleşmeleri imzalandı.
İhale şartnamesine göre muayene gelirinden Hazine'ye aktarılacak pay da kademeli olarak artacak: ilk 3 yıl yüzde 30, sonraki 7 yıl yüzde 40, son 10 yıl yüzde 50.
Sürücülerin muayene ücretini kartla öderken karşılaştığı komisyon uygulaması sona eriyor. Uraloğlu, 15 Ağustos 2027'de başlayacak yeni imtiyaz döneminde kredi kartı komisyonu alınmayacağını açıkladı. Bazı haberlerde bu düzenlemenin banka kartı ödemelerini de kapsadığı belirtiliyor.
Komisyonun kaybolması, bedelin ortadan kalktığı anlamına gelmiyor. Özelleştirme İdaresi Başkanlığı'nın ihale sürecinde duyurduğu şartlara göre kartlı ödemelerdeki komisyon vatandaşa yansıtılmayacak, bu ücreti yeni dönemde işletmeci firmalar karşılayacak.
Türkiye'de trafiğe kayıtlı araç sayısı 31 milyon 300 bini aşarken, muayeneye giren her sürücü için ödeme anındaki bu fark doğrudan cebe dokunuyordu.
Şu an 219'u sabit, 102'si seyyar olmak üzere 321 noktada verilen hizmet, yeni dönemde 249 sabit ve 103 seyyar olmak üzere toplam 352 istasyona çıkarılacak. Büyükşehirlerde 8 kanallı istasyonlar açılacak, motosiklet sahipleri için yalnızca iki tekerlekli araçlara hizmet veren özel istasyonlar kurulacak.
Hatların içi de değişiyor. İstasyonlarda süspansiyon test cihazları, elektronik boyut ölçüm sistemleri ve otomatik plaka tanıma altyapısı kullanılacak, ilerleyen süreçte OBD cihazları da devreye girecek. Yeni nesil hatlarda yapay zekâ destekli görüntü işleme, lazer tarayıcılar ve otomatik kusur tespit sistemi görev alacak. Elektrikli araçlara özel testler yapılacak, gelişmiş sürüş güvenliği sistemleri de muayene kapsamına alınacak.
Yatırımın toplam büyüklüğü 2,2 milyar dolar : 1,72 milyar dolarlık işletme hakkı bedeli ile 500 milyon dolarlık teknoloji ve istasyon yatırımı. Yeni dönemde yaklaşık 4.500 kişilik istihdam hedefleniyor, istasyonların afet ve acil durumlarda sahra hastanesi olarak kullanılabilecek şekilde tasarlanacağı da belirtildi. Yeni sistemin hızla işlemesi ve sürücülerin istasyonlarda daha az beklemesi bekleniyor.

Eski model Murat Mısırlı, yaklaşık 7 yıldır ALS hastalığıyla mücadele ediyor. Mısırlı'yı bu süreçte dostları yalnız bırakmıyor. Bir dönem mankenlik de yapan oyuncular; Kenan İmirzalıoğlu , Atilla Saral ve Burak Hakkı, Mısırlı'yı ziyaret etti. Yıllara dayanan arkadaşlığın buluşmasından fotoğraflar sosyal medyada paylaşıldı. Atilla Saral, fotoğrafa "Can arkadaşlar" notunu ekledi.
Murat Mısırlı, 1968 yılında İzmir'in Karşıyaka ilçesinde doğdu. İlkokul yıllarından itibaren sporla ilgilenen Mısırlı, gençliğinde tenis, judo ve hentbol dallarında amatör ve profesyonel olarak faaliyet gösterdi. İstanbul Üniversitesi'nde mühendislik eğitimi aldığı sırada gelen modellik tekliflerini değerlendiren Mısırlı, 1990'lı yıllarda Türkiye'nin tanınmış erkek mankenlerinden biri oldu.
Mısırlı, profesyonel dansçılık da yaptı. Yurt dışında düzenlenen organizasyonlarda Türkiye'yi 30 farklı ülkede temsil etti. Güzellik yarışmalarının ve defilelerin koreografi çalışmalarında görev aldı. Oyunculuk kariyerine de adım atan Murat Mısırlı, Levent Kırca Tiyatrosu'nda sahneye çıktı ve çeşitli televizyon dizilerinde rol aldı. Burcu Ergün Mısırlı ile evli olan eski mankenin Tibet adında bir oğlu bulunuyor.
Amyotrofik lateral skleroz ya da ALS, esas olarak istemli kas hareketinin kontrolünden sorumlu sinir hücrelerinin hasarından kaynaklanan nadir bir nörolojik hastalık grubudur. İstemli kaslar çiğneme, yürüme ve konuşma gibi hareketlerin yapılmasında görevlidir. ALS hastalığı ilerleyicidir ve belirtiler zamanla kötüleşme eğilimi gösterir. Günümüzde, ALS hastalığının ilerleyişini durdurmak ya da tam tedavi sağlamak için herhangi bir tedavi seçeneği yoktur ancak bu konudaki araştırmalar devam etmektedir.

Türkiye'de araç muayenesi yaptıran sürücülerin kredi kartıyla ödeme sırasında karşılaştığı ek hizmet bedeli uygulaması sona erecek. Ulaştırma ve Altyapı Bakanı Abdulkadir Uraloğlu, TBMM Plan ve Bütçe Komisyonu'nda Bakanlığının 2027 yılı bütçe görüşmeleri sırasında yaptığı açıklamada, yeni dönemde kredi kartı komisyonunun araç sahiplerine yansıtılmayacağını bildirdi.
Mevcut araç muayene işletme sözleşmesinin 15 Ağustos 2027 tarihinde sona ereceğini belirten Uraloğlu, yeni sistemin Ağustos 2027'de devreye alınmasının planlandığını açıkladı. Böylece sürücüler, muayene ücretlerini kredi kartıyla öderken ayrıca komisyon ödemeyecek.
Araç muayene ücretlerinin kredi kartıyla ödenmesi sırasında tahsil edilen ek hizmet bedeli, sürücülerin uzun süredir tepki gösterdiği konular arasında yer alıyor.
Daha önce Meclis gündemine de taşınan uygulamaya ilişkin Bakanlık tarafından verilen yanıtta, kredi kartı komisyon maliyetinin hizmet alan kişilere yansıtılmaması şartının yeni ihale şartnamesine eklendiği bildirilmişti.
Mevcut imtiyaz sözleşmesinin 15 Ağustos 2027'de sona ermesiyle birlikte yeni işletme dönemine geçilecek. Yeni sistemin devreye alınmasıyla kredi kartıyla ödeme yapan araç sahiplerinden ayrıca hizmet bedeli tahsil edilmeyecek.
Yeni sistemle birlikte araç muayene istasyonlarında teknolojik altyapının da yenilenmesi planlanıyor. Bu kapsamda muayene işlemlerinde yapay zekâ destekli teknolojilerden yararlanılacak.
Yeni uygulamayla araç kontrollerinin güvenilirliğinin artırılması, muayene süreçlerinin daha etkin yürütülmesi ve istasyonlarda yaşanan bekleme sürelerinin azaltılması hedefleniyor.
Yapılacak değişiklik, araç muayene ücretlerinin kaldırılması veya düşürülmesi anlamına gelmiyor. Düzenleme yalnızca kredi kartıyla ödeme sırasında tahsil edilen ek hizmet bedelini kapsıyor.
Buna göre sürücüler, Ağustos 2027'de başlaması planlanan yeni işletme döneminden itibaren muayene ücretlerini kredi kartıyla öderken ayrıca komisyon ödemeyecek.

Çocuk yıldız olarak başladığı kariyerinde hem televizyon hem sinema alanında birçok projede rol alan Hayden Panettiere, 36 yaşında 16 Ağustos'ta hayatını kaybetti.
ABD'nin Güney Carolina eyaletinde bir evde hareketsiz olarak bulunan ve olay yerine gelen sağlık ekiplerinin müdahalesine rağmen kurtarılamayan oyuncu, ölümünde herhangi bir şüpheli duruma rastlanmadığı belirtilmişti.
36 yaşındaki Panettiere'nin ölüm sebebi resmi kayıtlara kaza olarak geçerken, oyuncunun vefatının farklı maddelerin birleşen etkilerinden kaynaklandığı belirtildi.
Ukraynalı boksör Wladimir Klitschko ile ilişkisinden Kaya adında bir kızı bulunan Hayden Panettiere 'nin mal varlığı vefatından aylar sonra ortaya çıktı.
Kızının annesinin vefatı sonrası yasal işlemleri başlatan Wladimir Klitschko, mahkemeden oyuncunun servetini yönetmek üzere Melissa Moskal Bencivenga'nın mali danışman olarak atanmasını istedi.
TMZ'nin elde ettiği belgelerde Hayden Panettiere 'nin herhangi bir vasiyetname bırakmadığı yer aldı.
Yaklaşık 5,2 milyon dolar değerinde kişisel mal varlığı ve 1 milyon dolar üzerinde değere sahip gayrimenkulü olduğu öğrenilen oyuncunun toplam mirasının 6,2 milyon dolar (yaklaşık 316 milyon TL) olduğu ortaya çıktı.
Henüz bir yaşına gelmeden reklam filminde rol alan Hayden Panettiere, “One Life to Live” adlı diziyle oyunculuğa başlarken daha 4 yaşındaydı.
Çocuk yaşta başladığı oyunculuğa uzun yılldır devam eden Hayden Panettiere, Heroes dizisinde canlandırdığı Claire Bennet ve Nashville adlı dizideki Juliette Barnes rolüyle hafızalara kazındı.
Oyuncu, "Remember the Titans", "Raising Helen", "Ice Princess", “I Love You, Beth Cooper” ve "Scream" serisi gibi yapımlarda da rol aldı.
Mayıs 2026'da yayınlanan "This Is Me: A Reckoning" adlı anı kitabında çocuk yaşta şöhret olmanın zorlukları, geçirdiği depresyon ve bağımlılık süreçlerine dair samimi açıklamalarda bulunmuştu.
Öte yandan Panettiere’in kendisi gibi oyuncu kardeşi Jansen Panettiere de 2023 yılında, henüz 28 yaşındayken kalp büyümesi ve aort kapağı komplikasyonları nedeniyle hayatını kaybetmişti.

BBC'nin haberine göre, BBC'nin Rusça servisi Belaruslu Cyber Partisans BY grubu ve Ukrayna’dan Silent Crow tarafından gerçekleştirilen bir siber saldırının ardından, 2021’den Eylül 2026’ya kadar olan dönemde 11 milyondan fazla ölüm kaydına erişim sağladı.
Rusya Federal İstatistik Kurumu (Rosstat), siber saldırıyı kabul ederken, koruma altındaki bilgilerin sızmadığını öne sürdü.
Rosstat verilerini kendi verileriyle analiz ederek birleştiren BBC'nin Rusça servisine göre, 2022'deki başlangıcından Eylül 2026'ya kadar Rusya-Ukrayna Savaşı'nda 490 bin 334 Rus askeri hayatını kaybetti.
Ayrıca analizde 5 bin 17 yabancı askerin de Rusya için savaşırken yaşamını yitirdiği öne sürüldü.
Öte yandan BBC'nin haberine göre Ukrayna Devlet Başkanı Volodimir Zelenskiy, Temmuz 2026'da yaptığı açıklamada Ukrayna'nın asker kaybını 50 bin civarı olarak açıklasa da, "UA Losses" isimli internet sitesinde bu rakamın yaklaşık 115 bin olduğu iddia ediliyor.

texts.https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cqpv:
Hunter Schafer first came across Blade Runner when the 2017 sequel was released
"What does it mean to be human?" is a question that's always been at the heart of Blade Runner.
The first film in the series, released in 1982, depicted a technologically advanced yet dystopian version of Los Angeles in the then-distant future of 2019.
While the movie's flying cars haven't - quite - materialised yet in the real world, Blade Runner's themes of technological progress and the threats it poses feel just as relevant.
At least that's what the cast and crew of Blade Runner 2099, a new TV series set in the same universe, are hoping.
BBC Newsbeat spoke to stars Hunter Schafer, Lewis Gribben and Dimitri Abold, plus showrunner Silka Luisa, to ask why they think themes of artificial consciousness and existential threats still resonate.
The original Blade Runner, directed by Sir Ridley Scott, is considered a sci-fi classic that had a long-lasting influence on the genre.
It told the story of Detective Deckard, played by Harrison Ford, who hunted down synthetic humans known as replicants.
Schafer says her first exposure to the series was actually marketing for Blade Runner 2049 - the film sequel starring Ford and Ryan Gosling in 2017.
"I never thought I'd have the opportunity to make an addition to the world," she says.
"And so when that opportunity came along, I was quite thrilled."
Blade Runner 2099 is set 80 years after the original film, and portrays a Los Angeles where replicants have taken over.
Schafer plays Cora, a fugitive human forced to team up with replicant Olwen (played by Michelle Yeoh), as she tries to track down an artefact that could save humanity.
Schafer stars alongside Oscar winner Michelle Yeoh in the new TV adaptation
The series lands at a time when there are disagreements about the nature of the threat AI could pose to humans .
"I think it's particularly relevant right now, especially for the youth and young people who are inheriting a world that's asking a lot of the same questions that the show asks," says Schafer.
"I think that's timely and hopefully helpful to some degree."
But Blade Runner 2099 isn't "necessarily about just AI", says showrunner Luisa.
"It's this bigger question of what is the world going to be in 15 years and how can you plan for it?" she says.
The first Blade Runner also touched on themes of corporate greed and environmental damage, which are evident in the new series.
Luisa hopes the theme of a future that "is not going to be what you were promised" resonates with viewers today.
"The idea that you were born into a world and you thought you were expecting certain aspects of your life just to roll out," she says.
"That system is collapsing. And so what will be your place in whatever comes next?"
Blade Runner 2049 won awards and scored well with reviewers, but reports suggested it didn't hit box office targets.
This was partly blamed on marketing for the film trying to appeal more to existing fans than new ones - so what would the cast say to get younger viewers on board?
"It's just a very rich world," says Gribben, who plays Cora's younger brother Elias.
Gribben also points out that Blade Runner 2099, which employed "hundreds of artists and craftspeople" according to its makers, is a celebration of traditional film-making despite its themes.
"And I think studios will rely more on technology to make better-looking movies, but they won't have that soul."
Abold, who plays Cora's human ally Bebeto, says one of the show's key messages is about "the connections that you make".
"And the connections that you make are the foundation of humanity," he says.
"Because at the end of the day, all we have is ourselves and each other, right? And that's what feeds any human emotional experience."
Cora is helped by human allies including her brother Elias (Lewis Gribben) and Bebeto (Dimitri Abold)
Reviews for Blade Runner 2099 have been mostly positive, with a score of 72% on Rotten Tomatoes , external and an average of 65% on review aggregator Metacritic , external .
There was praise for the lead performances, the show's visual style and the way it updates the themes established in previous series entries.
The most common criticism was the show's pacing, with several critics describing it as a slow-burn and questioning whether Blade Runner worked as well off the big screen.
Schafer says she felt a lot of pressure when she signed up for the show,
"It's something that we were all aware of when making this show," she says.
"Most people who love film-making love Blade Runner, everybody brought their best to work.
Blade Runner 2099 is available on Prime Video from 25 November.
