A new book charts the complicated relationship between the two legends, starting on a sunny afternoon in Rio in 1979
P elé and Diego Maradona first met in April 1979, not long after the Argentinian led his country’s under-20 side to the finals of the World Youth Cup. Maradona told a journalist friend that his dream was to meet the Brazilian, and after a few weeks of aborted attempts to bring them together – mostly because Diego did not want to travel on a Monday, the one day he had free for his girlfriend Claudia – the meeting finally took place in Rio.
Reporter Guillermo Blanco, who was writing about the meeting for Argentinian sports magazine El Gráfico, got the OK from Pelé’s people and was so intent on making it happen that he checked Maradona onto a flight one Sunday night without telling him. He collared the young man after Argentine Juniors played Huracán and then raced to the airport and put him on a plane with his father, his agent and a photographer.
The next day, the small group of Argentines went to Alfredo Saad’s apartment in Copacabana, where Maradona and Pelé sat for an hour discussing football and life. ‘It was all great, they chatted, Pelé got out his guitar, he sang some songs, it was really nice,’ Blanco recalled. ‘Then there was a moment when it got a bit deep when Pelé started to give Diego some advice. He took Diego’s hand and he started giving him counsel. “Look after your body. Remember to always train. There’s a lot of responsibility on your shoulders.” It was like a premonition. Everything that would happen to Diego, Pelé, with all his experience, was telling him would happen.’ Before they left, Pelé hugged Maradona’s father and gave his son a signed ball, a Brazil shirt and a Pelé watch. The friendship between the players appeared to be sealed. ‘I knew Pelé was a God as a player,’ Maradona said. ‘Now that I’ve met him, I know he is as a person, too.’
Those present that sunny afternoon in Rio could never have imagined how the paths of the two men would diverge, overlap and collide, like wingers and full-backs determined to get the better of each other. Their mutual admiration survived for a few more years but when it soured, it soured royally and the fallout made headlines around the world. They were often described as rivals but what they really had was a love-hate relationship fuelled by South American nationalism and grandiose egos. Adding even more spice were the moralistic subtexts of good vs evil, the establishment vs the people, and the conformist vs the rebel. They were two completely different people and everyone took a side. Maradona summed it up perfectly: ‘We’re oil and water.’
The first cracks in their friendship appeared three years after their Rio meeting, when Pelé criticised Maradona’s performance at the 1982 World Cup. The Brazilian agreed to write a syndicated column during the tournament, and before it even kicked off he predicted that Zico would make more of an impact than Maradona. In a sentence that would drive the first wedge between them, he questioned not just Maradona’s ability but his character. ‘My biggest doubt,’ Pelé wrote, ‘lies in knowing if Diego has sufficient greatness in his person to justify the honours that the world audience pays him.’
Pelé’s scepticism turned out to be entirely justified. Maradona lost the plot in Argentina’s second-round match against Brazil and was sent off after stamping on Batista in the dying minutes of their 3-1 loss. The defeat meant the champions were out and Maradona, as Pelé predicted, had failed to live up to the hype. In his column the next day, Pelé piled on the misery, calling Maradona ‘an immature young man, who almost hasn’t had the time to transform himself into the great player that many people blindly state that he is’.
To Maradona, the words were a betrayal. He had considered Pelé a friend and an ally, and he never forgot how the Brazilian became one of the first major figures to cast aspersions on his talent and character. Maradona was hardly a paragon of loyalty – he fought with just about everyone who ever loved him – but he demanded fealty from everyone else and Pelé’s slight wounded him deeply. And yet it took a while for his anger to show. Maradona was just 21 and a long way from becoming the all-conquering superstar who would wow the world. He had opinions but he was still shy about speaking out, not yet sure how good he would really be. It was only after leading Argentina to victory in 1986 that his ego exploded and he started reacting to his critics. It was then, after the world united in appointing him as the successor to Pelé’s throne, that he began assailing everyone who questioned his greatness.
It took a while, but Pelé saw what was happening and he realised he had to react. He began defending his legacy and the rivalry between the two men was up and running. For almost his entire career, Pelé was recognised as the greatest footballer of all time. Rivals had come and gone but none posed a lasting threat to the coveted title. Peers such as Alfredo Di Stéfano, Eusébio and Johan Cruyff all had the talent to threaten his supremacy but they and their supporting casts were either not good enough or not consistent enough to keep their teams at the top for extended periods, especially at international level.
Maradona was different and Pelé knew it. He wasn’t just brilliant, he also played for a nation that produced enough quality players to help him win the titles he needed to be considered extra-special. Crucially, like few players before or since, he had both an aura about him as well as a gift for making the players around him better. He never won anything single-handedly, as many people liked to say, but when he was on form his teammates grew in stature and together they became more than just the sum of their parts.
His performances in leading Argentina to the World Cup in 1986 were so remarkable that Pelé started playing up his own achievements and subtly questioning those of his rival. While the rest of the world marvelled at football’s new messiah, Pelé would grumpily ask how anyone could compare him to a player whose most unforgettable goal was scored with his hand. Pelé’s misgivings were rooted in his own sense of right and wrong as well as the deep footballing history between their nations. Argentina’s World Cup win in 1986 was their second, and they were now just one behind Brazil, whose three titles had come a generation earlier. The gap between them was closing and Brazilians were worried. They felt they were the best in the world at the one thing that mattered and the thought that their neighbours might rob them of that honour was terrifying, particularly given the questionable manner with which they’d won both titles.
Brazilians always considered Argentines if not downright cheats then tricksters who revelled in taking liberties. It was a questionable attitude, given that Brazilians were no strangers to gamesmanship. When Argentines did it, they protested and called it cheating. When the Brazilians did it, they smiled and called it cunning. Maradona, of course, was typically Argentine in knowing when and how to bend the rules, but it wasn’t just his cheating that bothered Pelé. It was the unrepentant way he celebrated it. The doping, the handball against England , the drink and drugs, Pelé found it all tasteless and improper, and Maradona’s blasphemy made it doubly worse. His insistence on naming the first goal against England ‘the hand of God’ offended a man who took his faith seriously.
Epic: The many lives of Pelé by Andrew Downie is available now at the Guardian Bookshop .

Plus: the quickest team to go from FA Cup winners to the first round and matches delayed by snowball fights
“Ronaldinho played for Ravenna, in Serie C, earlier this month. It was his first professional appearance in more than 11 years,” writes George Jones. “Have any other footballers had long career hiatuses? And has any player had a longer hiatus than 11 years?”
Ronaldinho’s last professional appearance before his return for Ravenna came on 26 September 2015 for Fluminense, who won 2-0 at home against Goiás. He was withdrawn after 45 minutes. Fans of symmetry will be pleased to see that 11 years and 50 days later, the Brazilian returned for Ravenna in a 2-0 home win against another team with five letters and an accent in their name, Forlì, and was withdrawn after 45 minutes.
Considering he is now 46 and was playing against a team containing a couple of players 26 years his junior, his 25 touches, one key pass (in the buildup to the opening goal) and 81% passing accuracy in a single half is better than respectable. And nope, stats weren’t available for tracking back and we don’t imagine he ranked too highly on that metric … but he’s 46! Only time will tell if the World Cup winner plays again. “It was amazing,” he beamed after the match. “I got more than 30 minutes under my belt and feel good. I didn’t really want to come off. It was all over in a flash. I’m still not sure if this will be my only appearance, but if the president comes calling, I’ll be back.”
But back to the question. There have been a few high-profile returns following a player’s initial “retirement”. In 2012 Paul Scholes jumped back into Manchester United’s midfield seven months after hanging up his boots to help out amid an injury crisis and played for another 18 months, helping United to seal their 20th league title in May 2013. Arjen Robben resumed his career at his boyhood club, Groningen, a year after calling time at Bayern Munich.
A more curious example is that of the former Argentina goalkeeper Carlos Roa, who at his peak and aged 30, took a retreat from football to focus on his faith with reports suggesting he anticipated the year 2000 being the end of the world. A devout Christian, Roa went to live with his family in a secluded area of Argentina to prepare for the apocalypse. When it didn’t come, he resumed his career at Mallorca a year after his last appearance but never played for the national team again.
But these tales get us nowhere near to Ronaldinho. Gareth Barry had a four-and-a-half-year hiatus between his retirement as a professional at West Brom in 2020 and his return to playing again at Hurstpierpoint in the Mid Sussex League Championship in February 2025 – not at professional level but still pretty competitive. Jürgen Klinsmann made a similar return to playing at amateur level five years after “retiring”. Klinsmann scored on his farewell appearance for Tottenham in a 1-1 draw with Southampton on the last day of the 1997-98 Premier League season. However, aged 39, he came back under the pseudonym “Jay Göppingen” and scored five goals in eight appearances for Orange County Blue Star, a team in the Premier Development League (then the fourth tier of the US pyramid).
Maybe Ronaldinho was inspired by his former World Cup-winning teammate Denílson signing for Íbis Sport Club in 2022, 12 years after his retirement. However, the then 44-year-old never made an appearance for the lower-league Brazilian club, with the signing seemingly a publicity stunt for a club often dubbed the “worst in the world” after going three years, 11 months and 26 days without a win in the 1980s.
Which takes us to another brilliant Brazilian. The late, great Sócrates came out of retirement on 20 November 2004 aged 50, 15 years after his last appearance for Botafogo on 12 November 1989. He signed a one-month player-coach deal with Garforth Town, on the outskirts of Leeds, in the Northern Counties East Football League and played 12 minutes at the end of a 2-2 draw with Tadcaster Albion. “It was far too cold; the second I got out there I had an incredible headache. I’m just not used to it,” he gasped after the match. “But I really enjoyed it and it was an interesting experience.” His appearance drew huge crowds to tiny Wheatley Park and came about because of a shared interest in football coaching schools for children which the owner, Simon Clifford, was trying to promote.
The hiatus for Sócrates stands at 15 years and eight days, four years greater than that of Ronaldinho, though perhaps Ronaldinho’s ability to step back into the third tier of a professional league and more than hold his own is a more impressive achievement. What is unarguable, though, is their status as two Brazil greats.
The former Scotland defender Neil McBain had a playing hiatus longer than the two legends above, however. “McBain started his career as a half-back for Ayr United in 1915,” writes Robin Horton. “He retired in 1931, as player-manager for Watford, by which time he was playing centre-half, his last game being an FA Cup tie at Birmingham on 14 February. By 1946 he was in charge of New Brighton.”
“On 15 March 1947, with the club suffering a goalkeeping crisis, and with four players – including chosen keeper Corbett – failing to turn up for a match at Hartlepool United, McBain himself donned the green jersey. The Rakers duly lost 3–0, although the first goal was a shot ‘which might easily have caused Frank Swift’s eyes to boggle’. At 51 years old, he was the oldest player ever to play in the Football League – 16 years, one month and one day from his previous appearance.”
“Are Leicester City the quickest team ever to go from winning the FA Cup to playing in the FA Cup first round proper?” asks Ricardio Sentulio.
Leicester won the FA Cup in 2021 , when Youri Tielemans scored a spectacular winner against Chelsea at Wembley in front of a post-Covid crowd of 20,000. As any fule kno, they’re now in League One after back-to-back relegations. That meant an early start in the FA Cup: on 6 November, to be precise, when Leicester won 4-2 at Oxford City.
They’re not the first team to plunge from winners to first-round entrants in the space of five years, though. As Rhys Shakeshaft points out, until 1925 the winners began their defence in the first round as a matter of course. That included Tottenham Hotspur , who won the competition as a non-league team in 1901.
Since 1925, when the top clubs were first given a bye to the third round, two teams have suffered a faster descent than Leicester.
“ Portsmouth won the FA Cup in 2008 ,” writes Michael Haughey, “and dropped into League One in 2012 four seasons later.” But, as Alicia Butteriss and others point out, Wigan went from champions to first-round entrants in half that time.
They famously beat Manchester City in the FA Cup final of 2013 , the same year in which they were relegated from the Premier League. Two years later, they dropped another level into League One. On 7 November 2015, precisely 910 days after Wigan beat City at Wembley, they played Bury away in the first round. Bury won 4-0.
“Is the incident involving CSKA Sofia and Levski Sofia the first time a match has ever been delayed by a snowball fight?” wondered Nathan Fisher in 2014 .
Nope, it isn’t Nathan. On 19 December 2010, Larissa fans took advantage of a rare snowfall in Greece to hurl missiles at Olympiakos’s Vasilis Torosidis , now of Roma of course. Went down like a sack of potatoes. On the same day in Belgium, Anderlecht’s Jonathan Legear and Mbark Boussoufa came under heavy fire from Club Brugge fans with the referee forced to take the players back to the dressing room for seven minutes before the game restarted. Anderlecht went on to beat their rivals 2-0 , with Legear pelting his own fans in celebration, much to the displeasure of a Club Brugge steward who shoved the Belgian player. Bayern initially aim to find young players from Bavaria before looking further afield
Bayern Munich are one of the elite powers in European football and current home of Ballon d'Or winner and England captain Harry Kane.
But, while Kane is the latest hugely successful foreign import at Bayern, the German giants also put a particular focus on producing their own elite young talent.
In 2013, Bayern had four homegrown players in the starting line-up as they won the Champions League.
Repeating that victory, and continuing the club's history of nurturing young players, is what director of youth development and campus Jochen Sauer says Bayern are aiming for.
Sauer joined from Red Bull Salzburg in 2017 when the academy campus opened in another part of Munich, away from the first-team training complex.
The club's motto "Mia San Mia" translates to "we are who we are" and Sauer says it has always been the club's goal to have a local homegrown element in its senior side.
"It was always our identity and philosophy to be a regional club, but at the same time to be competitive internationally and on Champions League level," Sauer tells BBC Sport.
"But always having a core of our team coming from the Munich area and the Bavarian region with a deep identification with the club and the city.
"Our recruitment guidelines, especially for the under-11 to the under-15 teams, is trying to recruit as much talent as possible from the Munich area and the region of Bavaria."
Munich-born Croatia international Josip Stanisic is a good example. The midfielder, 26, signed as an under-17 player from local outfit SC Furstenfeldbruck, while 22-year-old Aleksandar Pavlovic joined the academy aged eight and has worked his way up to the first team and is a Germany international.
But perhaps the biggest name to come out of the academy in recent times is Jamal Musiala. The former Chelsea youth player, who joined aged 16, is a star for Bayern and Germany and has already won six Bundesliga titles at just 23 years old.
It was part of the club's strategy to bring in the best young foreign players, and those with German passports, to the club, but they also enjoyed a bit of luck.
The move came around the time Bayern Munich were interested in then-Chelsea winger Callum Hudson-Odoi, who shared the same agent as Musiala, who moved from Germany to England when he was seven.
Bayern were already aware of Musiala because he was born in Germany, but the timing was right to make a deal happen.
"There were for sure some pieces that came together at that time," Sauer says.
"I think one reason why we fought for the player at that time was the reason we had the feeling that Chelsea is not really seeing his full potential to be a top player for their first team.
"Because, otherwise, if they would have seen him as a future prospect, then it would been hard, even for Bayern Munich, to get a player out of the Chelsea environment."
Other young players in the first-team squad include 18-year-old Bara Sapoko Ndiaye, signed from Gambinos Stars Africa in The Gambia, and 18-year-old Lennart Karl, who joined the academy four years ago and has been capped by Germany.
Shirts with Bayern's academy graduates adorn the walls of their youth campus
The Bayern Campus can house up to 43 players in accommodation, predominantly local players before they widen the search overseas.
"I think there is basically kind of a guideline that we want to have a minimum 60% of the players coming from the region and reaching the level of the under-19 age group," Sauer says.
"This automatically means that the other 40% of the team has to be recruited from other regions nationwide.
"Coming to an age group of under-17, we are also reaching out to the main European football markets to recruit the most talented players internationally.
"Jamal Musiala is one perfect example. As soon as we're coming to an age of 16 and the regulations allow us to do international transfers, we want to recruit the best talents in Europe. That's for sure part of our recruitment philosophy."
Another piece that fell into place for Musiala was the Bayern under-17 team at that time was coached by Miroslav Klose, the former Bayern forward who is the record goalscorer for Germany.
Klose is credited with pushing Musiala to work on the defensive side of his game. He also knew what a player needed to get to the highest level, with the former striker becoming an assistant to Hansi Flick when Musiala joined the first team.
That idea of having former players in charge of the next generation continues.
Ex-Bayern centre-back Dante, who also played for Nice for more than 10 years, is the current under-19 head coach.
"They can inject a little bit of the Bayern Munich DNA into the players," Sauer explains. "More from a personality side, not necessarily from a playing style.
"He also has some different ideas on the playing style but you know playing for Bayern Munich and being in the first team of Bayern Munich, at least they can tell our players what they have to be from a character, from a personality to make it up to the first team."
With so many players coming into the system and a difficult first-team set-up to break into, the Bayern style remains consistent throughout age groups.
Coaches are given guidelines to work towards but it does not stop them from having their own ideas as they aim for a style of "dominance and intensity".
"But football is always a process of evaluation," Sauer says.
"Opening the campus in 2017, we have put a very clear idea of football in place, but always kept the openness to add in ideas from coaches like [Jupp] Heynckes, [Julian] Nagelsmann, [Thomas] Tuchel, Hansi Flick, and, for sure, [current Bayern manager Vincent] Kompany. The football is always developing.
"So we have to be open enough always to amend little things. But I would say that the overall strategy is still what it was in the times of Heynckes, Pep Guardiola or Louis van Gaal."
There is an eye-catching display in one of the well-kept corridors of Bayern's campus. Shirts of high-profile academy graduates are framed on the walls, with a display showing tiers of Germany's football leagues and players who have played in them.
To qualify for the display, players need to have played a minimum of 30 full 90-minute games.
Bayern say that almost 44% of the young players who are in their youth set-up until the under-19 team become a professional player.
"The success is not only bringing players to Allianz Arena, but bringing players also to professional football. This is also essential if you want to convince a young talented player to be part of Bayern Munich," Sauer adds.
"For us, it's more the story: Listen, if you're coming to Bayern Munich we cannot guarantee that you will be a first-team player at Bayern Munich, because it's very tough to achieve. And you have a lot of world-class players around you. So if you are a top striker and you have Harry Kane there it will be difficult to replace him.
"But what we can at least guarantee you is we can teach you and develop you to a level that you have a very, very big chance to be a professional football player at least in a tier one, tier two or tier-three club."
Like most things in modern football, the development of players also has to make business sense for the six-time European champions, who last won the Champions League in 2019-20.
"Being in a competition with Paris St-Germain, all the English and the Spanish clubs to win the Champions League, it would be almost unrealistic to say we want to have 11 players on the pitch that play for our academy," says Sauer.
"But I think if we can reach the goal that we always have five or six players steadily in the first team, that would be a great success.
"On the other side, and this is more I would say economical answer, we do not have the money of the English clubs. We do not have the TV money. To be still competitive over the next decade, I think we all also have to make money with our players."

Brüksel, yeni çağdaş ve modern sanat müzesi Kanal-Centre Pompidou'yu açmaya hazırlanıyor. Paris'teki Centre Pompidou işbirliğiyle hayata geçirilen müze, yüzlerce sanat eserine ev sahipliği yapacak. Açılış kapsamında Türk sanatçı Banu Cennetoğlu'nun insan haklarına dikkat çeken yerleştirmesi de ziyaretçilerle buluşacak.
Brüksel, uluslararası sanat merkezlerinden biri olma hedefi doğrultusunda yeni müzesini açıyor. Eski bir Citroen otomobil fabrikasının dönüştürülmesiyle oluşturulan Kanal-Centre Pompidou, hafta sonundan itibaren genel ziyaretçilere kapılarını açacak.
Paris'in dünyaca tanınan Centre Pompidou'su ile ortaklaşa yönetilecek müze, Henri Matisse, Alberto Giacometti ve Pablo Picasso gibi modern sanat tarihinin önemli isimlerinin yüzlerce eserini ağırlayacak.
Brüksel Bölge Hükümeti Başkanı Boris Dillies, müzenin açılışının Belçika başkentini New York, Londra ve Bilbao gibi önemli sanat kentleriyle aynı lige taşıyacağını söyledi.
Belçika kraliyet ailesinin de katılacağı resmi açılış töreni perşembe günü düzenlenecek. 1930'lu yıllardan kalma eski Citroen binasında kurulan müze, kanal kıyısındaki konumuyla dikkat çekiyor. Brüt beton yüzeyler, metal kirişler ve yüksek cam tavanıyla endüstriyel mimari özelliklerini koruyan yapı, kent manzarasına da geniş bir görüş sunuyor.
Müzenin açılışında ziyaretçileri Türk sanatçı Banu Cennetoğlu'nun hazırladığı altın renkli balonlardan oluşan yerleştirme karşılayacak.
Yüksek sütunlar halinde düzenlenen eser, 1948 tarihli İnsan Hakları Evrensel Beyannamesi'nin 30 maddesine gönderme yapıyor. Cennetoğlu'nun çalışması, müzenin ilk sergisinin sürgün, göç ve sınırlar etrafında şekillenen temalarıyla da örtüşüyor.
Kanal'ın koleksiyonu, Centre Pompidou ile 2031'e kadar sürecek 13 milyon euroluk bir anlaşma kapsamında yönetilecek. Anlaşma, yüzlerce sanat eserinin müzeye ödünç verilmesinin yanı sıra büyük ölçekli sergilerin düzenlenmesini de içeriyor. Paris'teki Centre Pompidou ise yenileme çalışmaları nedeniyle 2030'a kadar kapalı kalacak.
Müzenin ilk sergisinin öne çıkan eserlerinden biri, Alberto Giacometti'nin ünlü heykeli Yürüyen Adam olacak. Heykelin yakınında ise Fransız Yeni Dalga akımının fotoğrafçı ve yönetmenlerinden Agnes Varda'nın 1960'larda Küba'da çektiği fotoğraflar sergilenecek.
Pablo Picasso, Henri Matisse ve Man Ray gibi sanatçıların yanı sıra Franco-Cezayirli sanatçı Kader Attia'nın eserleri de müzenin koleksiyonunda yer alacak. Centre Pompidou Direktörü Xavier Rey, açılış sergisinin farklı dönemlerden ve sanat anlayışlarından isimleri bir araya getirdiğini belirtti.
Sürgün, göç ve sınır temalarına odaklanan ilk sergide Belçikalı sanatçı Joelle Tuerlinckx'in geniş bir bodrum alanında hazırladığı ışık ve ses yerleştirmesi de bulunuyor. Müzenin gelecek programında ise Fransız avangart sanatçılar Sonia ve Robert Delaunay'ya adanacak retrospektif sergi yer alıyor. Serginin Kasım 2027 ile Nisan 2028 arasında düzenlenmesi planlanıyor.
Kanal yalnızca bir sanat müzesi olarak değil, daha geniş kapsamlı bir kültür merkezi olarak tasarlandı. Çocuklar için oyun alanı, restoranlar, barlar ve bir mimarlık merkezinin yanı sıra atölyeler, film gösterimleri ve konserler düzenlenmesi de hedefleniyor.
Ancak yaklaşık 10 yıldır hazırlıkları süren proje, 300 milyon euroluk maliyeti nedeniyle eleştirilerin odağında. Özellikle kamu bütçesindeki kısıtlamalar nedeniyle kaynak sıkıntısı yaşayan diğer kültür kurumları, müzeye ayrılan bütçeyi sorguluyor.
Kanal Genel Müdürü Yves Goldstein, projenin hazırlık sürecinin kolay geçmediğini kabul ederken müzenin ölçeğini savundu. Goldstein, yapının ne devasa ne de aşırı büyük bir proje olduğunu, aksine ihtiyaç duyulan ölçekte tasarlandığını söyledi.
Buna karşın Brüksel yönetimi, müzeye sağlanan kamu desteğini kademeli olarak azaltmayı planlıyor. Yıllık finansmanın 2027'de 24 milyon eurodan 2029'da 10 milyon euroya düşürülmesi öngörülüyor. Müze yönetimi ise yaklaşık 30 milyon euroluk bir bağış fonu oluşturmayı hedefliyordu.
Bölge yönetimi başkanı Dillies, kamu kaynaklarının kullanımında mali disiplinin önemine dikkat çekerek yeni yönetimin özel sektörle ortaklıklar geliştirmesini umduğunu ifade etti.
Müzenin açılışına iki gün kala salı günü düzenlenen basın ziyaretinde inşaat çalışmalarının henüz tamamlanmadığı görüldü. Merdivenler, matkap sesleri ve çeşitli makinelerin arasında gazetecileri karşılayan yetkililerden Dillies ise devam eden inşaat çalışmalarının Brüksel'in başkent olma halinin bir parçası olduğunu esprili bir dille dile getirdi.

A Milli Erkek Basketbol Takımı, İtalya ve İzlanda maçlarına önemli oyuncularından yoksun çıkacak.
Ağustos ayındaki son pencere müsabakalarında forma giyen basketbolculardan kaptan Cedi Osman, sakatlığı nedeniyle aday kadroda yer alamadı. Amerikan Basketbol Ligi'nde (NBA) görev yapan Alperen Şengün ile Adem Bona kadroya çağrılmazken NBA Gelişim Ligi'nde oynayan Ömer Faruk Yurtseven ise aday kadroda bulunmasına rağmen sahada olamayacak.
Millilerde Yiğitcan Saybir ile Yavuz Gültekin, sakatlıkları nedeniyle aday kadrodan çıkarıldı.
Başantrenör Ergin Ataman, Anadolu Efes'in Basketbol Avrupa Ligi'nin 14. haftasında Kosner Baskonia ile deplasmanda oynayacağı maç nedeniyle Ercan Osmani'den de İtalya karşısında faydalanamayacaklarını açıkladı.
A Milli Erkek Basketbol Takımı'nın İtalya ve İzlanda maçları aday kadrosunda yer alan oyuncular şöyle:
Yiğit Onan (Aliağa Petkimspor), Ercan Osmani, Erkan Yılmaz (Anadolu Efes), Kenan Sipahi, Malachi Flynn, Furkan Haltalı (Bahçeşehir Koleji), Berk İbrahim Uğurlu, Furkan Korkmaz, Metecan Birsen (Beşiktaş), Egehan Arna (Esenler Erokspor), Onuralp Bitim, Sertaç Şanlı (Fenerbahçe Tarfin), Şehmus Hazer (Galatasaray MCT Technic), Yiğit Arslan (Trabzonspor), Doğuş Özdemiroğlu (Türk Telekom), Ömer Kutluay (Real Madrid), Ömer Faruk Yurtseven (Rio Grande Valley Vipers), Rüzgar Öpçün.
İtalya Milli Basketbol Takımı, J Grubu'nda 3. sırada yer alıyor.
Dünya Kupası Elemeleri'nde ilk turu 5 galibiyet ve 1 yenilgi sonucunda lider bitiren İtalya, ikinci turda henüz maç kazanamadı.
"Maviler" ağustos ayındaki müsabakalarda Bosna Hersek ile Sırbistan'a mağlup oldu.
Luca Banchi'nin başantrenörlüğünü yaptığı İtalya, Türkiye'yi mağlup ederek ikinci turda ilk galibiyetini almaya çalışacak.
"Maviler" grubu ilk 3'te tamamlayarak Dünya Kupası bileti almayı hedefliyor.

Batum kentindeki Batum Stadı'nda oynanacak müsabaka, TSİ 20.45'te başlayacak.
Müsabakayı Danimarka Futbol Federasyonundan hakem Morten Krogh yönetecek. Krogh'un yardımcılıklarını Victor Skytte ve Steffen Bramsen üstlenecek.
Avrupa Ligi'nde bu sezon 2 galibiyet, 1'er beraberlik ve yenilgi yaşayan siyah-beyazlı futbol takımı, topladığı 7 puanla haftaya 8. basamakta girdi.
Beşiktaş, Hapoel Beer-Sheva'yı mağlup ederek ilk 8 sıra iddiasını güçlendirmeyi hedefliyor.
Siyah-beyazlılarda yarınki Hapoel Beer-Sheva maçı öncesinde tek eksik oyuncu bulunuyor.
Beşiktaş'ta üçüncü haftadaki Crystal Palace karşılaşmasında gördüğü kırmızı karttan dolayı iki maçlık cezası süren Ümit Akdağ, Hapoel Beer-Sheva karşısında da görev yapamayacak.
Beşiktaş'ın yıldız futbolcuları Dusan Vlahovic ve Leandro Trossard, son haftalardaki performanslarıyla ön plana çıktı.
Siyah-beyazlı takımın Sırp santrforu, Süper Lig'de hafta sonu oynanan Konyaspor mücadelesinde 2 golle galibiyete katkı sağladı. Bu sezon Avrupa kupalarında ve ligde toplam 15 maça çıkan Vlahovic, 11 gol kaydetti.
Ligde son olarak Konyaspor ağlarını havalandıran Trossard ise bu sezonki gol sayısını 3'e çıkardı. Belçikalı futbolcu, son haftalarda hücumda gösterdiği etkili oyunla taraftarın alkışını alıyor.
Siyah-beyazlı takımın rakibi Hapoel Beer-Sheva, bu sezon UEFA Avrupa Ligi'nde 1 puan topladı.
İsrail ekibi, oynadığı 4 maçta 1 beraberlik, 3 yenilgi yaşadı ve haftaya 33. sırada girdi.
Rakip fileleri 1 kez havalandıran Hapoel Beer Sheva, kalesinde ise 8 gol gördü.

Bordo-mavili takım, Avrupa kupalarında daha önce oynadığı 160 müsabakanın 58'inden galibiyetle ayrıldı. 63 karşılaşmada mağlup olan Karadeniz ekibi, 39 kez de rakipleriyle berabere kaldı.
Trabzonspor, ilk olarak 1976-1977 sezonunda başladığı Avrupa serüveninde Şampiyon Kulüpler Kupası/UEFA Şampiyonlar Ligi'nde 30, UEFA Kupası/UEFA Avrupa Ligi'nde 99, Avrupa Kupa Galipleri Kupası'nda 12, UEFA Intertoto Kupası'nda 8 ve UEFA Konferans Ligi'nde 11 maç oynadı.
Bordo-mavililer, bu müsabakalarda 200 gol atarken kalesinde 217 gol gördü.
Trabzonspor, CSKA Sofya ile oynayacağı maçla UEFA Konferans Ligi adıyla düzenlenen Avrupa'nın 3 numaralı kupasında 12. kez sahne alacak.
UEFA Konferans Ligi'nde ilk olarak 2021-2022 sezonunda Norveç'in Molde takımıyla karşılaşan bordo-mavililer, bu organizasyonda oynadığı 11 maçın 3'ünü kazanırken, 4'ünde berabere kaldı, 4'ünü ise kaybetti.
Bu maçlarda rakip fileleri 13 kez havalandıran Trabzonspor, kalesinde de 15 gol gördü.
Bordo-mavili takım, bu sezon Avrupa'da altıncı karşılaşmasını oynayacak. Karadeniz ekibi, UEFA Avrupa Ligi play-off turunda Macaristan'ın Ferencvaros takımına sahasında 1-0, deplasmanda 4-0 mağlup oldu.
Trabzonspor, UEFA Konferans Ligi ilk hafta maçında Finlandiya'nın KuPS Kuopio takımını deplasmanda 4-2, sahasında İskoçya'nın Hearts takımını 2-0 yenerken Almanya'nın Freiburg takımına evinde 1-0 kaybetti.
Trabzonspor, ilk kez bir Bulgar takımı ile karşı karşıya gelecek.
CSKA Sofya ile yapılacak UEFA Konferans Ligi karşılaşması bordo-mavili ekibin ilk kez bir Bulgar takımı ile oynadığı karşılaşma olarak kayıtlara geçecek.
